stories.title: Knicks to decline Pacome Dadiet's fourth-year option
stories.summary: The Knicks are set to decline Pacome Dadiet's fourth-year option, making the former first-round pick an unrestricted free agent in June.
stories.detailText: The Knicks are planning to decline former first-round pick Pacome Dadiet 's fourth-year option, SNY's NBA Insider Ian Begley confirms. New York's move will make Dadiet an unrestricted free agent next June and create salary space heading into the 2027-28 season. Dadiet, who was selected 25th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft, has been unable to carve out playing time with the Knicks since he arrived. The French national appeared in 18 games his rookie season, where he averaged 1.7 points on 32 percent shooting. He averaged the same amount of points on 33 percent shooting across 29 games last season. This season, the 21-year-old has appeared in one game, grabbing one board in his one minute on the court.

stories.title: LeBron James looked all 41 years of his life on these highlight plays
stories.summary: LeBron James was on the wrong end of a crossover and chasedown block to finally look old
stories.detailText: LeBron James is essentially outlasting every elite athlete in the history of sports by playing his 24th season for the Philadelphia 76ers this year. James turns 42 years old in Dec., and if he fulfills the second year of his contract next season, he will have played 10 more seasons than Michael Jordan. James’ peak wasn’t as high as MJ’s by most models , but he’s trying to win the GOAT debate on longevity, and he’s certainly made it a worthwhile discussion. Father Time doesn’t lose, and that’s even the case against a freak of nature like LeBron. James showed some signs of age on Wednesday night as his 76ers needed a big fourth quarter comeback just to get by the Indiana Pacers without Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac. James was solid in the win with 13 points, 10 assists, five rebounds, and three stocks, but he was also on the wrong end of two highlight plays that the internet is still talking about a day later. Early in the second quarter, James was speeding down the court for what should have been a fastbreak dunk. Instead, Indiana’s Jalen Slawson, who is only on a two-way contract, beat him to the rim for the chasedown block. He did a LeBron to LeBron! Watch the play here: JALEN SLAWSON CHASEDOWN BLOCK 😤 pic.twitter.com/OMB0kg8squ — Indiana Pacers (@Pacers) October 28, 2026 LeBron was never caught from behind for years and years and years. There’s only so much he can do before he turns 42, though, and this time another super athlete like Slawson got the best of him. Look at Slawson talk trash to LeBron at the end of that clip. Have some respect for your elders, young man! I say this as a big Slawson fan, he was on my ‘too good for Summer League’ list this year. As if that wasn’t ba enough, LeBron got got even worse late in the fourth quarter. Pacers guard Andrew Nembhard squared up James and hit him with a dirty crossover that sent the 40-something tumbling. Nembhard missed the shot, so this clip isn’t as humiliating as it could have been. NEMBHARD ANKLE BREAKER ON LEBRON 😭 pic.twitter.com/FQIjF5Gi57 — Basketball Performances (@NBAPerformances) October 29, 2026 The Sixers came back and won to improve to 4-1 on the year. That’s great. LeBron has stayed durable while so many other players have gone down with injuries early this season, and he’s poised to be a key piece of a team with championship aspirations come playoff time. Everything LeBron is doing at this age is crazy, but he’s still showing plenty of signs of slowing down. The end is near, but LeBron is fighting for his athletic life unlike anyone we’ve ever seen before.

stories.title: Timberwolves' Anthony Edwards undergoes successful knee scope
stories.summary: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic on Thursday, the team announced.
stories.detailText: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, on Thursday, the team announced. Edwards had a debridement procedure performed on his knee, which is a minimally invasive measure used to clean, smooth or remove damaged cartilage, bone spurs or loose joint fragments from the knee joint to relieve pain and improve mobility, according to the Mayo Clinic. The team's statement said Edwards is expected to make a full recovery but did not denote a time frame for his potential return. Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that Edwards could be sidelined up to two months . Speaking before Wednesday night's loss to the Warriors, Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly said he expects Edwards to be "good as new" when he eventually returns to game action . Edwards, 25, has been bothered by right knee pain since last spring and was limited to a career-low 61 games last season. He was seen grabbing his knee and grimacing at one point during Sunday's home opener against the Toronto Raptors . Even after being listed as questionable to play Monday, Edwards scored 47 points in an overtime loss at Cleveland . His 133 points through four games is a franchise record. An MRI on Tuesday revealed new damage for Edwards that was not detected in previous scans, which were done before training camp and during the playoffs. His condition this summer was not such that a procedure would have been recommended then, Connelly said Wednesday. "We're just concerned about his long-term health," Connelly added. "We want to make sure we're putting him in the best position he can be so he can be the best version he's going to be for a long time. "He's bummed, but Anthony is such a naturally positive and upbeat guy. He's hit all his teammates quickly and said, 'You guys got it,' and we'll roll from there." Wolves coach Chris Finch said before Wednesday's loss to Golden State that the Edwards news was "a bit of a shock to everybody." Finch, however, feels confident that his team has the depth and experience to navigate an extended stretch without Edwards. "We'll have to kind of fill that scoring void by committee," Finch said. "Certainly, spreading more shots around the team, everybody likes that. Obviously they've got to go in to make up the point difference." Information from the Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.summary: The veteran forward helped key a win for the undermanned Lakers on Wednesday

(Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Across the first four games of the regular season, Jarred Vanderbilt found himself entirely outside of the Los Angeles Lakers’ rotation, with head coach JJ Redick opting for Sandro Mamukelashvili and Kevon Looney as his backup big men behind Walker Kessler. But Looney struggled mightily in those appearances. His insufficient scoring and passing were stunting the offense while his lack of size and declining mobility rendered him an issue defensively. So, Redick gave Looney’s rotation spot to Vanderbilt against the Los Angeles Clippers Wednesday night and the veteran forward, in his first minutes of the season, delivered. His motor, range and quickness defensively caused problems and the Lakers outscored the Clippers by 22 points during his 21 minutes. In particular, Redick cited Vanderbilt’s ability to front the post against Brook Lopez as a crucial contribution . Following the victory, Collin Sexton — who previously spent half a season alongside Vanderbilt with the Utah Jazz in 2022-23 before Vanderbilt was dealt to Los Angeles — praised Vanderbilt’s even-keeled mentality while he rode the bench early on and how his approach benefits the whole team. “Vando is somebody that is always going to stay ready … You never see any bad days for Vando. He’s always going to be a leader,” Sexton told reporters. “He’s always going to come in and be that vet and be that good person whether he plays no minutes or he plays 48 minutes. He’s always going to be the same person and I feel like that’s one of the things that helps in the locker room is we’re all for the team and tonight, he was definitely for the team. He came in and he brought that juice right away and I feel like he was a huge, huge impact in us winning.” Given Vanderbilt’s impressive 2026-27 debut and Looney’s poor showing through four games, it seems pretty likely Vanderbilt will continue garnering rotation minutes for the time being. His next chance comes Friday on the road when the Lakers kick off their NBA Cup Group Play against the Golden State Warriors at 7 p.m. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: “Yak is our starter,” but here’s what Rajaković’s centre rotation might look like
stories.summary: While Poeltl’s starting job seems safe, Trayce Jackson-Davis’ heroics might have earned him a bigger opportunity to come
stories.detailText: TORONTO, CANADA - MARCH 7: Trayce Jackson-Davis #32, Jakob Poeltl #19 and Head Coach Darko Rajakovic of the Toronto Raptors participates in an all access practice on March 7 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Vaughn Ridley/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images “Yak is our starter. We’re number one defence in the league at this time, and he, Yak, has a lot to do with that.” This is the stance of Raptors coach Darko Rajaković after the Toronto team’s first four games in the season. In them, Jakob Poeltl, that Raptors’ starting centre, has averaged three points, four and a half rebounds, and less than one block per game, in just under 20 minutes a game. This is a far cry from Yak’s near 15-10 season back in ‘24-’25, and the injuries that have plagued Poeltl in the years since have contributed heavily to two seasons (thus far) of very limited production from the big man. Nevertheless, Rajaković refuses to publicly condemn his player. “Yak does so many things on defensive end of the ball that it helps us tremendously,” the coach said at today’s presser. “And lot of those things, they will not show up in the box-score you know, and the way he’s presenting himself in the paint, the way he’s controlling screener, the way he rotates and helps our guys… Offensively, I think his rhythm is gonna come.” While overreacting to a small sample size is unhelpful, it is clear as day that some type of issues are present. Whether lingering injuries remain a concern, or something else is keeping Poeltl at bay, something needs to change for the Raptors if they want to win games in the modern NBA. And, while Rajaković remains steadfast, standing by the Austrian big man, he has also insinuated that he is not burying his head in the sand, and may be choosing to address this issue from a rotational perspective at this juncture. the raps can keep starting jak if they want to, i don't care too much about that. but the minutes distribution at centre is gonna have to change. soon. — Joe Wolfond (@joey_doubleyou) October 26, 2026 Journalist Joe Wolfond seems to have cleanly summed up the direction the Raptors may be taking the team, as the coach indicated that the Raptors’ current arrangement of centre minutes was not set in stone. “Everything is on the table, you know?” Rajaković said when asked about Trayce Jackson-Davis getting more minutes at the 5. “Obviously, I love to have as many players as possible to be ready to help us and to step on the floor. It’s just finding those right moments, right minutes and the right rotations to maximize that.” While relatively non-committal, this statement suggests that Rajaković may be exploring what having the 6’9” centre play a bigger part in the Raps’ rotation could look like. And if last night is any indication, that looks good. In a game where both Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray Boyles got into f0ul trouble , Jackson-Davis stepped up to grab 11 rebounds, and looked like a ray of hope for the Raptors. TORONTO, CANADA – OCTOBER 21: Caleb Wilson #8 of the Chicago Bulls drives to the basket against Trayce Jackson-Davis #32 of the Toronto Raptors in the second half of their NBA game at Scotiabank Arena on October 21, 2026 in Toronto, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Cole Burston/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jackson-Davis is two inches taller than Collin Murray-Boyles, and the two of them off the bench may combine to give the Raptors that extra support at the 5 that is so necessary, but cannot be sustained at this juncture by Poeltl and Boyles alone. With the Raptors facing off against the Orlando Magic again this Friday, the team will have another opportunity, both to give Jakob Poeltl time to demonstrate that he is a starting-calibre centre, and for Trayce Jackson-Davis to show both the organization and the fans that he needs more minutes.

stories.title: Hawks First Week Recap: Positives and negatives
stories.summary: Observations from the first week of play.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 28: Kingston Flemings #4 of the Atlanta Hawks reacts after a dunk past Dru Smith #12 of the Miami Heat during fourth quarter at State Farm Arena on October 28, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last night, the Hawks were looking to end their back-to-back losses to the Houston Rockets and extend the offensive funk for the Miami Heat, who hadn’t won a game heading into the matchup. Rather than reclaiming a winning record however, the Hawks became the Heat’s first win of the season and fell to 2-3, with all three losses coming one after another. This game also officially concluded the first week of the season for the Hawks. While a season is certainly not won or lost in the first week, there are several positives and negatives for the Hawks to take away from their first week of action. Positive: Turning steals into points Thanks in large part to the expected defensive brilliance of Dyson Daniels, the Hawks rank fourth in the league in total steals. Not only are the Hawks ending possessions, but they are converting forced turnovers to points on the other end. The team ranks fourth in points off turnovers as well. A large part of the scoring is their ability to push in transition and convert, ranking in the top five in fastbreak points. The Hawks are composed of tenacious defenders and talented ball handlers, which are ingredients in the perfect recipe for pushing the envelope in transition. This trend being a part of their identity will make them a dangerous team going forward. Negative: Interior Play If you’ve watched any of the three losses for the Hawks this season, you’ve probably noticed they are putting on their best matador impression in the painted area. In the three losses, they’ve been significantly outrebounded (147-117) and outscored in the paint (172 versus 164). At one point, in the second matchup against the Rockets, the Hawks were being outrebounded 14-4. The Heat scored 70 points in the paint, which was more than half of their total scoring output. Averaging the third fewest blocks in the league, the Hawks offer defensive resistance down low that is similar to using a piece of scotch tape to prevent a truck from driving through your house. If this trend continues throughout the season, the Hawks will put a heavy burden on their offense that may not be sustainable. Positive: Emergence of Kingston Flemings After losing Trae Young last season, the Hawks greatly needed another point guard. That need led to drafting Kingston Flemings with the eighth overall pick in the draft. Coming off the bench, Flemings struggled in his first game, going scoreless on 0-for-5 shooting. Despite the early woes, his performance against the Heat was just the beginning of what the former five-star is capable of. Flemings scored 23 points on 9-for-12 shooting, which included shooting 3-of-5 from deep. Along with the scoring output, Flemings grabbed five boards, dished five assists, along with a steal and a block. He had a sequence of back-to-back buckets, which included an “and-one” finish, a block on a much taller Giannis Antetokounmpo, and an even more impressive finish over the future first-ballot hall of gamer. Flemings also found himself in the game down the stretch as the Hawks tried to rally a fourth quarter comeback before the effort eventually flamed out. Though it’s early in the season, it seems that Flemings could be the point guard of the future for Atlanta. Negative: Slow start for Jalen Johnson If you looked at only points, rebounds, and assists for Jalen Johnson, it would be fair to assume he was continuing his dominance from last season. In their first matchup against Houston, Johnson channeled his inner John Stockton and tallied a staggering 16 assists along with 26 points and nine boards. However, the averages have not translated to impacting winning in the same way. The biggest detractor for the former Duke Blue Devil is his less-than-ideal shooting percentages. He is shooting 42.8% from the field, which is well below the area a team’s number one option should be. Johnson has only posted a field goal percentage above 45% once, which was his 19 points on 9-for-16 shooting in their huge win over Charlotte. His past two outings featured shooting 35.7% and 33.3%. Despite these poor numbers, his three-point efficiency is the most frightening part. Johnson’s career high in assists against mentioned above is higher than his three-point percentage, which currently sits at 15.8%. If the Hawks want to make another playoff push, Johnson has put the ball in the basket at a more efficient clip. Positive: Productive scoring back court Despite Jalen Johnson’s slow start, the Hawks are still receiving great support from their back court. Nickiel Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum once again are proving to be the Hawks’ go to options for offense. ‘NAW’ is the team’s only guy to score 30 so far, which was in the opening game against the Magic. He’s also shooting 38% from three, proving to be a reliable option from behind the arc and seems to convert when his team needs it most. McCollum is the Hawks’ undisputed microwave scorer, seeming to get hot quickly and put up points in a hurry. The 14-year veteran is shooting an impressive 53% from the field and 44% from three. There are times when it seems like McCollum simply cannot miss, which provides a huge boost to the Hawks. The duo averages a combined 36.1 points per game, which is more than ideal for second and third scoring options. Aaron Wiggins has also been critical off the bench. Whether it be catch-and-shoot opportunities or creating his own shot off the dribble, Wiggins is averaging 15.8 points per game on 53.5%/48% shooting splits, which is the perfect spark of the bench for Atlanta. Negative: Three-point shooting In today’s NBA, three-point shooting is undoubtedly a team’s biggest weapon. For the Hawks, the three-point shot is one of their biggest deficiencies. In their last games, which again, are all losses, they have the second lowest three-point percentage in the entire league. In the second Houston matchup, the Hawks shot 28% as a team, which included their bench only shooting 3-for-15 for the game. One of the most startling revelations of their three-performance comes from the center position. Ideally, teams with bigs shooting at a high frequency spread out a defense and open up opportunities for an offense to execute at all levels of the floor. However, when your centers are shooting 4-for-32 on the season from behind the arc, that vision is difficult to achieve. With their defensive and rebounding issues, the Hawks will have to counter with big scoring outputs, which can only be achieved with improved three-point shooting.

stories.summary: A trio of Lakers reserves stepped up in a big way Wednesday night
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 28: Sandro Mamukelashvili #54 and Jarred Vanderbilt #2 of the Los Angeles Lakers goes up for the rebound during the game against the LA Clippers on October 28, 2026 at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Playing the second night of a back-to-back following a narrow loss to the Portland Trail Blazers, the Luka Dončić-less Los Angeles Lakers were going to need some unsung heroes to help them topple the Los Angeles Clippers Wednesday night. That became even more apparent as Austin Reaves struggled through his worst outing of the season, going 6-of-16 from the floor, scoring 16 points and committing eight turnovers — the first time in five games he’d shot worse than 54.5% or tallied fewer than 23 points. Reaves and the shorthanded Lakers found reinforcements from their bench trio, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jarred Vanderbilt, all of whom helped Los Angeles handle the Clippers, 103-87 , for a fourth win in five tries this season. Sexton recorded a season-high 21 points (6-of-11 shooting, 4-of-7 from deep), four rebounds and two assists. Mamukelashvili filled up the box score with 13 points (6-of-15 shooting), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. Vanderbilt made his regular season debut, chipping in seven rebounds and two assists; although he did not score, his motor and range defensively helped stymie the Clippers’ frontline. “I think the guys, Vando, Sexton, Mamu, those guys, you can’t always read into like the single-game plus-minus, but very apparent in our good stretches of the game, just the impact that those guys had,” head coach JJ Redick told reporters postgame. “They ended up with [a plus-minus of] +21, + 23 + 22, those three guys off the bench. They were great. They helped us win. In particular, the Mamukelashvili-Vanderbilt tandem produced good results for the Lakers, which outscored the Clippers by 27 points (51-24) across the 20 minutes those two played together. Redick acknowledged their complementary skill-sets — Vanderbilt’s defensive signature and Mamukelashvili’s offensive versatility — as the driving force behind that success. “It was good. We had Vando on Lopez. He did a great job. We showed a clip at halftime of fronting him in the post and not allowing him to get the basketball,” Redick said. “Vando’s always going to play hard. He’s always going to impact the game with just his effort and I thought he did that tonight. The pairing with Mamu, it’s probably the best pairing in terms of having another big out there that can space and shoot and playmake.” You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: How the NBA’s injury onslaught could help—and hurt—the Sixers
stories.summary: The Sixers could bank some early-season wins thanks to injuries around the NBA, but those injuries could lead to some long-term financial consequences.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 19: Tyrese Maxey #0 of the Philadelphia 76ers and Tyrese Haliburton #0 of the Indiana Pacers talk after the game on January 19, 2026 at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Barely one week into the 2026-27 NBA season, a handful of teams are dealing with season-altering injuries. Thunder wing Jalen Williams (fibula/ankle) and guard Cason Wallace (shoulder) may already be out for the season . Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard is “ expected to miss a period of weeks ” because of swelling in his left knee. Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards may be out for two months because of a knee injury. A torn MCL is set to sideline Jazz big man Jaren Jackson Jr. for 6-8 weeks . Magic forward Paolo Banchero is out for multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain, while guard Jalen Suggs is out for at least two weeks because of a bone bruise in his right knee. And Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton is out for at least two weeks due to a left hamstring strain. Those are the major ones, although other teams throughout the league are dealing with various bumps and bruises as well. The Pacers, whom the Sixers faced on Wednesday, were without both Haliburton and starting center Ivica Zubac (ankle), which helped the Sixers escape with a 114-109 road win. The Sixers are dealing with a handful of injuries as well, although all five of their starters are healthy for now. As long as that remains the case, they’re poised to take advantage of these other absences throughout the league. The Sixers don’t play the Thunder, Jazz or Timberwolves until the calendar flips to 2027, so Edwards and Jackson might be back by then. (J-Dub and Wallace likely won’t be back for either of the two Sixers-Thunder games in January and February.) However, the Sixers will host the Raptors on Nov. 12 and head to Orlando six days later, which means they could avoid Leonard and Banchero in those games. They also host the Pacers on Nov. 15 and face them again on the first night of a back-to-back in late November, so they might dodge Haliburton in at least one of those games if not both. Head-to-head results aside, those injuries could prove costly to their respective teams in terms of their win-loss record. And with the East looking especially cutthroat this year, an early-season slide from the Magic and/or Raptors might leave the Sixers with fewer competitors for a top playoff seed. That would be a welcome development, particularly given how much the Sixers might need to load-manage Joel Embiid and LeBron James throughout the regular season. However, the leaguewide wave of injuries could have one notable long-term consequence for the Sixers. After this season, Tyrese Maxey will have seven years of NBA experience and will have two years left on his contract. If he doesn’t make an All-NBA team this year, he’ll be eligible to sign a three-year extension next summer starting at 30 percent of the 2029-30 salary cap. If he does make an All-NBA team, he’ll be eligible to sign a four-year extension starting at 35 percent of the 2029-30 salary cap. Those back-to-back All-NBA nods would also automatically qualify him for a five-year supermax extension in 2028, too. Maxey made the All-NBA third team last year, in part because stars like Edwards, Stephen Curry and Giannis Antetokounmpo weren’t eligible for end-of-season awards since they played in fewer than 65 games. Edwards will likely be ineligible again this season, and Leonard and Haliburton are already in danger of losing their eligibility as well. And again, it’s only the first week of the season. More All-NBA candidates are bound to miss time moving forward. Heading into the season, it was fair to wonder whether the Sixers’ new star-studded starting five would all cannibalize one another’s production, jeopardizing their chances at All-Star and All-NBA nods. However, through the first five games of the season, Maxey is averaging 28.4 points on 46.2 percent shooting, 4.6 assists and 4.2 rebounds per game. He’s doing all of that while shooting only 32.4 percent from deep, a figure which is bound to come up in the near future. Maxey was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week for the first week of the season. He was the only player in the NBA to average at least 25 points, two steals and one block per game over that span, according to the Sixers . If he maintains anywhere near that level of production moving forward and plays in the requisite 65 games, he’ll be in strong contention for an All-NBA nod, if not an outright lock. Luckily, Maxey is already on a guaranteed contract through 2028-29, so his supermax eligibility wouldn’t impact the Sixers until 2029 at the earliest. However, both Embiid and Jaylen Brown’s contracts are set to expire after the 2028-29 campaign as well—provided, of course, that Embiid picks up his $67.3 million player option for 2028-29—while VJ Edgecombe will become a restricted free agent in 2029 if the Sixers don’t sign him to an extension by the rookie-scale extension deadline in October 2028. That’s a lot of overlapping pieces to juggle. Again, none of that is a concern this season. All the Sixers need to focus on this year is coalescing and getting 1 percent better every day, as Maxey is fond of saying. But if this early-season wave of injuries does increase Maxey’s probability of earning his second straight All-NBA nod, it could create some long-term financial consequences for the Sixers as early as next summer. How they navigate those will help shape the next era of Sixers basketball after LeBron either leaves or retires. Unless otherwise noted, all stats via NBA.com , PBPStats , Cleaning the Glass or Basketball Reference . All salary information via Spotrac and salary-cap information via RealGM . stories.title: Praying for the healthy Knicks as we approach Día de Muertos
stories.summary: The injury bug is bitting hard early in the NBA season. Somehow, the Knicks keep escaping Santa Muerte.
stories.detailText: Relatives watch over their dead in the cemeteries of the Nahuatl community of San Isidro Buensuceso, in the town of San Pablo del Monte, to continue the tradition of the Dia de Muertos. They gather in the graves of their dead where they are put on candles, food and they sing all night until the dawn of November 2 to welcome their loved ones. on November 2, 2019 in Tlaxcala, Mexico (Photo by Eyepix/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images It’s not even Halloween, the NBA season is barely a week old, but the injury report already looks like something you’d expect to read in April. Here in Mexico City, I can relate. You can feel Día de Muertos in the air, both figuratively and literally. We’re just days — hours, if you push it — away from one of the biggest festivities in the country to take place this weekend. No need to explain what we celebrate, trying to bring back those who left us in the past to start just another chapter away from the land. If only for a little ratito . View this post on Instagram Meanwhile, in the NBA, it looks like stars are playing a very solid role in a performance mimicking this weekend’s celebrations. It’s not a few, but muchos , who have already undergone surgery and be placed on the shelves for months on end, if not the whole year, outright. Meanwhile, the New York Knicks are doing something that is starting to feel illegal, some sort of subterfuge competitive advantage in itself. Being healthy. Vivito y coleando . Keerthika Uthayakumar’s little research went viral yesterday. Yet according to ESPN’s injury report from early Thursday, the Knicks had just one player listed: my man José , who missed the game against the Chicago Bulls with an ankle injury. Maldito tobillo. Now compare that with the rest of the league, where approximately 15 percent of players (s/o Keerthika!) were dealing with injuries or illnesses yesterday afternoon. Eleven former All-Stars were already expected to miss several weeks or longer just eight days into the season. 79 players are listed with an injury or illness on today's 2:30 PM injury report, for games that are on tonight's schedule. That's approximately 15% of the NBA!! https://t.co/IUAEnOrQmE — Keerthika Uthayakumar (@keerthikau) October 28, 2026 The NBA injury report is a hot parrillada Obviously, the most concerning situation might be in Oklahoma City, where Jalen Williams underwent surgery to repair a fractured left fibula and reconstruct ankle ligaments following a fracture-dislocation and will only be reevaluated by the team when the regular season ends . Gone for good, in other words. Descanse en paz, bendito. His teammate Cason Wallace also needs surgery after tearing the labrum in his left shoulder, and both will miss a hellaciously long time. Minnesota’s Anthony Edwards underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right knee and could miss two months. Utah’s Jaren Jackson Jr. tore the MCL in his right knee and faces a six-to-eight-week absence. Indiana’s Tyrese Haliburton, already coming off a season lost to an Achilles injury, will miss at least two weeks with a hamstring strain. Orlando’s Paolo Banchero faces four to six weeks out with a high ankle sprain, while Toronto’s Kawhi Leonard is expected to miss multiple weeks because of swelling in his left knee. Elsewhere, Golden State is without Jimmy Butler III until potentially January or February, while Kristaps Porzingis remains away indefinitely with ongoing health concerns. Sacramento’s Ben Simmons and former Knickerbocker Ariel Hukporti suffered Achilles ruptures, and Washington’s Jamir Watkins is recovering from ACL surgery. Hay más almas que cempasúchil en el sendero . Somehow, the Knicks have avoided all of this As Stefan Bondy of the New York Post noted, every member of the Knicks’ starting five reached the 65-game threshold in both 2024-25 and 2025-26. Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, and Karl-Anthony Towns have provided a level of continuity that most teams can only dream about. ¡Quién pudiera! Bridges hasn’t missed an NBA game in his career even though seemingly everybody wants him hitting the pine for a start, with his streak reaching 643 consecutive appearances on Wednesday. Towns and Anunoby, meanwhile, arrived in New York with considerable injury histories but have remained remarkably durable. Per Bondy, the Knicks’ starting five led the NBA with 940 minutes together in 2024-25, finished second with 541 last season, and ranked first again through four games this year. stories.title: ‘He’s putting it all together ’: Evan Mobley’s leap could be upon us
stories.summary: Mobley is knocking down three-pointers at a career-high rate.
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 26: Evan Mobley #4 of the Cleveland Cavaliers celebrates after scoring during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Rocket Arena on October 26, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. The Cavaliers defeated the Timberwolves 127-125 in overtime. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers have waited for a significant offensive leap from Evan Mobley. Subtle improvements over the years have refined him into being an elite two-way player. But that next step was always a question mark. Would it be developing a mid-range game, or a go-to move around the basket? Or would Mobley step outside the three-point line and become a good enough shooter to open the floor for Cleveland? Right now, it sounds like the third option. Mobley has opened the season shooting 12-for-18 from downtown (66%). This is a blistering number that won’t be sustainable throughout 82 games — but it could mark the start of a career-best year. “I felt it in preseason, leading up to preseason,” said Kenny Atkinson. “There’s a shift in his demeanor… He put in the work. There’s a confidence to him now. It’s raised.” Mobley took six three-pointers on Wednesday against the Washington Wizards and nailed five of them. He had similar success in Cleveland’s win over the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this week, canning 4-of-5 attempts with three of his triples coming in the fourth quarter and overtime. Evan Mobley: 9 3PM in his last 7.5 quarters. Shooting with confidence. Very little hesitation. One fluid motion. Small sample size, but very encouraging early on #LetEmKnow pic.twitter.com/MePFrfzcWc — Mikey McNuggets (@MikeLucasTV) October 29, 2026 It’s one thing to take a three-pointer as a last resort. It’s another to launch them confidently even when the game is on the line. This is something Mobley began flashing in last season’s playoffs, but has taken to another level to start the year. “I think last year he’d kind of make 3s with time and space. I feel like this year he’s getting it off quicker. He’s making them with harder contests,” said Atkinson. “We saw it last year in the playoffs too, right? Detroit series, hit some big ones. Toronto series, hit some big ones. When a guy’s in a groove like this, we’ve got to find him a little more.” Mobley, always nonchalant, says his hot-shooting is simply a result of his work ethic. “Just confidence,” said Mobley. “The first few went in, so I just kept shooting them. Been working on them for years now. I feel confident in it, and I’m gonna keep shooting them.” The three-point shot is arguably the most valuable offensive tool a player can add to their game. Especially in the frontcourt. Cleveland has managed for years to navigate the lack of shooting in their frontcourt — but that awkward spacing might not be such a thorn in their side if Mobley can step outside and make defenses pay. “He’s just putting it all together,” said Jarrett Allen. “It opens the floor up to me. There’s not a lot of people in there, so I can do my work in there.” Nearly all of Mobley’s three-point attempts have been products of the defense sagging off him. In each of his last two games, Rudy Gobert and Anthony Davis made a deliberate choice to ignore Mobley in favor of packing the paint. It was on Mobley to punish them for this decision, and he did. “If they keep playing like that, I’m gonna keep shooting it,” said Mobley. “So, until they close out really hard, I’m gonna just keep letting it fly.” Still, there’s pressure on Mobley to stick to his greatest strengths as a play-finisher around the basket. He’s spent more time on the perimeter than we’ve grown accustomed to. The increased shooting is great, but the Cavs don’t want Mobley to rely too heavily on it. “I still want him at the paint, at the rim, just finding that balance,” said Atkinson. “I think [his shooting] opens things up for us. He’s taking timely ones. He’s taking good ones. If he can hit 3s and still be the great defender he is and should be, that could be our next jump.” There’s a lot of season left and plenty of time for Mobley’s shooting to regress. That said, Mobley has given himself a strong foundation to build on. A full season of Mobley taking and making threes could change everything.

stories.title: NBA's biggest surprises, most concerning starts and best teams of the early season
stories.summary: Our writers share their takeaways from the first week-plus and power-rank the five best teams so far.
stories.detailText: It's already Day 10 of the NBA season! What have been the biggest surprises so far? Most concerning starts? Under-the-radar developments? Our writers weigh in on the first week-plus of play and power-rank their five best teams in the early going. What's been the most pleasant surprise of the season? Tom Haberstroh: Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and the Portland Trail Blazers bringing the joy back to Rip City. After a tumultuous summer of financial cuts and political infighting, the basketball — that actual sport by which everything revolves — could not be more refreshing. Dame Time is back, Ja Morant has arrived and Deni Avdija is flourishing. Steve Jones: The Trail Blazers. Ja Morant has played with joy and hustle, getting to his spots with drives and cutting to make defenses pay for helping. Damian Lillard's ability to be used on- and off-ball has opened up a ton. There's a consistent energy boost from Jrue Holiday, Robert Williams III, Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson that keeps the Blazers consistent. Every year there is a team that shows early buy-in that turns into success; the Blazers have worked to answer offseason questions. Dan Devine: The Grizzlies, who opened 4-0 after not having a single four-game winning streak all of last season . It obviously starts with Ty Jerome getting enough minutes and touches to make all that math matter , but there's also: Cam Boozer walking into the NBA as a 15-10-5 guy even without his shot falling; Cedric Coward and Jaylen Wells shooting the cover off the ball as young wings; Zach Edey and Isaiah Stewart leading the league's best interior-rim-protecting unit ; etc. Trading away Ja Morant, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Desmond Bane made Memphis feel like a team in the midst of a full-tilt rebuild, but it was also one of the most injury-ravaged teams in the NBA last season . Give 'em a clean bill of health and an instant-impact rookie, and the Grizz might be a hell of a lot better than we thought. Kelly Iko: The Rockets. A team that has floundered near the bottom in half-court offensive efficiency for years is fourth courtesy of an absolutely lethal Fred VanVleet pick-and-roll approach. Houston has been able to quietly take the ball out of Kevin Durant's hands more, lessening the creation and decision-making pressure he was left with last season, and simplified some of Alperen Şengün's choices (a career high in scoring efficiency). It's still quite early in the season for longevity purposes, but it's been a welcome change. Who has had the most concerning start to the season? Iko: The Heat. Miami's win over Atlanta felt like a must-win, which is concerning in itself. But for this particular group, boasting some of the most versatile defenders around, to be 27th in efficiency is shocking. A frontcourt led by Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo is fifth in opponent rim rate (and conversion), but is getting torched on the perimeter. Davion Mitchell isn't generating the same pressure he typically does, Klay Thompson is an absolute shell of himself defensively and things move a bit sluggishly on that end of the floor altogether. This looks more like a play-in team than a noisemaker in the East, and that's concerning given the offseason resources exhausted. Haberstroh: Players' bodies. Anthony Edwards, Kawhi Leonard, Jalen Duren, Paolo Banchero, Jalen Williams, Tyrese Haliburton, Jaren Jackson Jr., Brandon Ingram, Ben Simmons. That's nine current or former All-Stars who are out for the foreseeable future due to their bodies breaking down. And that's just the tip of the iceberg. Jones: The Nuggets, because of my expectations for how they would build on last year. It may not matter as the wins are likely to stack up, but their defense can't be this for them to find their highest level of success, especially if the offense isn't hitting all the right notes. Fix one, get it done, get back off to the races. Devine: The Kings. It's not exactly a surprise; I think everyone expected them to be very bad. But they are 0-4, have already lost two games by 25 or more points, and are getting outscored by more than 16 points per 100 possessions . Several potential rays of sunshine — Ben Simmons, Maxime Raynaud, Keegan Murray, Dylan Cardwell — are already out injured. Rookie point guard Darius Acuff is on pace to become the first rookie to take 20 shots a game in 50 years , which would be fine if he weren't missing two-thirds of them. Domantas Sabonis is averaging 19-17-7 on 72% shooting and it just, like, doesn't matter? At all? Asked how a team in Sacramento's position might turn it around, Zach LaVine rattled off some of the key factors: strong organizational leadership from up top, an on-court floor general, an experienced veteran head coach. And then he straight up said, "We don't really have any of that right now, and it's not going to come anytime soon." Which, y'know: Yikes! Which under-the-radar development deserves more attention? Jones: The Mavericks finding a way to build an offense that highlights Cooper Flagg's strengths, takes nothing away from what Kyrie Irving brings to the table and opens things up for everyone to play a role. Their work to move the ball, to have actions running on both sides, and to blend cuts and dribble penetration has stood out early this season. Also, who is ready for Brandon Miller, Most Improved Player? Devine: The Raptors have nearly as many steals (57) as turnovers (60) through their first four games, and are forcing opponents to cough the ball up on nearly 22% of their offensive possessions . No team has finished a season with a rate above 19% in the 23 years for which Cleaning the Glass has opponent turnover data. And this is with Kawhi Leonard playing two games without looking at all like himself before going on the injured list, and with Toronto giving more minutes to veteran Jakob Poeltl than young doomsday device Collin Murray-Boyles (which I would expect to change sooner rather than later). If the Raptors go from a top-seven defense to the NBA's best defense, they become a hell of a lot more dangerous as a postseason threat — especially if Kawhi comes back moving and shooting better after his early-season siesta. Iko: Alperen Şengün is attempting over two 3s a game — and connecting on over 60% of them! When we talked about ways Houston's '70s-style offense could improve, one less-heralded note was Şengün becoming more comfortable taking outside shots, whether as a trailer or because defenses are showing crowds. I think it's more important that he simply takes the shots than his ability to convert them, which doesn't take away from what the Rockets do overall offensively. Haberstroh: Ty Jerome and the Memphis Grizzlies. I get why people are skeptical this can last — the potential for injury derailing everything looms large as does the soft schedule making them look better than they are. But Jerome is the breakout star of the season and his supporting cast is way better than advertised. (You should read about Jerome's long-awaited breakout .) Power-rank the five best teams in the NBA so far. Devine: 1. Rockets, 2. Sixers, 3. Thunder, 4. Lakers, 5. Knicks Houston's undefeated with top-five units on both ends, bolstered by Fred VanVleet's return. Philly's defense has been surprisingly sensational to start, and while its 27th-ranked offense is still ironing out the kinks, Tyrese Maxey looks like a legit MVP candidate. Oklahoma City's obviously feeling the pain of the brutal injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, but Shai Gilgeous-Alexander plus that defense plus a scintillating start for Ajay Mitchell has them up near the top for me. Ditto for the Lakers, who've gotten red-hot starts from a top-two offense led by Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, to go with a league-average defense — exactly the formula they need to contend. Yes, the Knicks opened the season 0-3, and yes, their starters (outside of Karl-Anthony Towns) are still thawing out their jumpers. But after taking care of the Pistons and scoring 77 second-half points to beat the Bulls on the road on the second night of a back-to-back, it seems like the offense is getting unstuck, which makes me feel OK about giving the champs the benefit of the doubt for the final spot here. Iko: 1. Rockets, 2. Pistons, 3. Sixers, 4. Blazers, 5. Grizzlies Houston is healthy and flowing. Cade Cunningham continues to be the straw that stirs the drink and Ausar Thompson has relaunched his bid for DPOY early (as has his twin brother in Houston). Philly is an absolute blur in transition (when generating stops) and might need to lean into that as opposed to the benefits of bringing four offensive stars together. stories.title: Clippers host sparks online war over whether she farted live on air — decide for yourself
stories.summary: A viral clip of Los Angeles Clippers in-arena host Hannah Cormier's hot mic mishap during the Lakers game is sparking controversy.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Clippers might not have been the only thing that stank in the Intuit Dome last night. The Clippers fell to 1-3 after their 103-87 loss to the Lakers on Wednesday night. However, a moment involving their in-arena host is getting the most attention. Los Angeles Clippers in-arena host Hannah Cormier reacting to a mishap during a game against the Los Angeles Lakers. (X/@MattWallace888). Hannah Cormier is entering her fifth season with the Clippers organization and second as the in-arena host and MC. She was on camera during one point in the game, appearing to not realize they were rolling. She seemed to notice a few seconds later, which sparked a terrified look on her face. Los Angeles Clippers in-arena host Hannah Cormier reacting to a mishap during a game against the Los Angeles Lakers. (X/@MattWallace888). She gathered herself quickly before saying, “Clipper Nation, the ladies are back performing to ‘Gemstone’. Give it up for our Clippers spirit!” As Cormier walked away, the microphone caught a sound that sounded conspicuously like a fart. An X user posted a video of this entire debacle with the caption, “NBA reporter farts, stumbles over her words, walks off”. The clip has gone viral, amassing over 390,000 views in about 10 hours. NBA reporter farts, stumbles over her words, walks off pic.twitter.com/yL1TwQrRlH — Matt Wallace (@MattWallace888) October 29, 2026 Baba Miller #18 of the LA Clippers looks on during the game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California, Wednesday, October 28, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images There is some debate about what the sound actually was. Some believe it was truly Cormier passing gas that was caught on the microphone, while others are claiming is was either microphone static or something else the microphone inadvertently picked up. Fans can come up with their own conclusions about what the sound was. Regardless, this mic’d up mishap provided a welcome distraction to the Clippers’ mediocre on-court product .

stories.title: Jaylen Brown takes the high road in response to debunked trade demand rumor
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown said his piece about the Jayson Tatum video. Now, he’s ready to move on.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - OCTOBER 28: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Philadelphia 76ers looks on during the game against the Indiana Pacers on October 28, 2026 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Luther Schlaifer/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images It’s understandable that Jaylen Brown was not happy when the Boston Celtics sent him to a bitter rival. Brown’s name had come up in trade rumors multiple times over the last few years. After the team failed to land Giannis Antetokounmpo this past offseason — with Brown and his salary going to Milwaukee to make it all work — it seemed like the damage had been done. Brown was seemingly shopped to just about every team in the league. After 10 years, five All-Star selections, two All-NBA nods and a Finals MVP, the Celtics were trying to pack him up, as Brown put it. So, you could imagine Brown’s surprise when he was ultimately traded to the Sixers, a franchise he tortured often while in Boston. While Brown was diplomatic when asked about his time with the Celtics during his introductory presser in Philly, you could tell feelings lingered. He revealed that he still hadn’t spoken to Jayson Tatum, his All-Star teammate of nine years, since the trade broke. Recently, Tatum posted an interview to YouTube where he recollected the moment Brown was traded. Brown obviously didn’t think Tatum was being truthful and commented. Jayson Tatum on the Jaylen Brown trade in a recent interview: "I was just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world." Jaylen Brown in the comments: 🧢 pic.twitter.com/dia6lscJ2E — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) October 23, 2026 Even if Brown didn’t comment, you’d have to be awfully naive to believe Tatum. You’re telling me Brad Stevens made a blockbuster trade that could change the entire trajectory of the franchise … and his star player found out the same time as the rest of the world? Yeah, cap is fair. Tatum downplayed Brown’s comments, saying there was no beef . That led to Brown’s colorful response about lamb chops and gravy while also pointing out Tatum has a “great PR team.” A petty response? For sure. But it was a fun moment and, at that point, it seemed like everyone was ready to keep it moving. Then Brian Scalabrine had to insert himself into the situation. Scalabrine reported then recanted (kind of, sort of, but with a lot of arrogance) that Brown “demanded” a trade. Multiple reports have debunked that being the case, but that wasn’t a remedy for Scalabrine’s main character syndrome. He took it to the broadcast to insult Brown again. So, he reported something that wasn’t true, awkwardly recanted it, then sort of doubled down for his dislike of Brown. Scalabrine mocked the idea of doing PR for Tatum … while actively doing PR for Tatum . He spent five years with the Celtics as a player and has been working on Boston’s basketball broadcasts in some capacity since 2012. His loyalty is obvious. Just last year, he was doing PR work trying to get Brown in the MVP conversation. Now, he’s discrediting the season Brown had in 2025-26. That’s why Brown’s response to Scalabrine was a smart one. When it’s Brown vs. Tatum, that’s real drama with a potential payoff when the two play each other for the first time. Having beef (or lamb chop) with a pom-pom waving commentator is a losing battle. Jaylen Brown to reporters in Indy: “I never had any issue with scal I love scal. … I never demanded a trade, never made a list of ultimatums.” pic.twitter.com/ROHGJ5ifhz — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) October 29, 2026 If you viewed his response to Tatum as petty, this was the exact opposite. Brown took the high road, despite Scalabrine laying it on pretty thick over the last week or so. It makes Brown look like the bigger person and Scalabrine look silly. We still have to wait until Nov. 10 to see Brown go up against Tatum and his former team — and we have to wait all the way until January to see Brown’s return to Boston. Whether it’s beef or lamb chops with gravy, it should be fun.

stories.title: Nikola Jokic records 200th career triple-double in Nuggets' win over Pelicans
stories.summary: Denver's Nikola Jokic had 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists for his 200th career triple-double Wednesday night as the Nuggets beat the Pelicans. He needs 10 more to supplant the retired Russell Westbrook as the NBA leader.
stories.detailText: Nikola Jokic had 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists for his 200th career triple-double in the regular season, and the Denver Nuggets never trailed in a 104-91 victory over the winless New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night. Jamal Murray scored 23 points, and Aaron Gordon added 15 points and 11 rebounds for the Nuggets, who swept a two-game, home-and-home series with New Orleans. After overcoming a 23-point deficit to beat the Pelicans in Denver on Saturday, the Nuggets this time raced to a 22-point lead in the first half and maintained a comfortable margin most of the way. Zion Williamson scored 25 points for the Pelicans, hitting a fourth-quarter 3 that pulled New Orleans as close as 88-83. Murray responded with a 3 and a driving finger roll to push the Nuggets' lead back to 10. Jokic needs 10 more regular season triple-doubles to supplant Russell Westbrook, who retired after last season, as the NBA leader. Westbrook reached 200 triple-doubles in his 1,175th game; Jokic did it in his 814th. They are the only two players in NBA history to eclipse 200. Sixteen of Jokic's triple-doubles have come against the Pelicans, six more than any other opponent. Christian Braun scored 15 points and Trevon Brazile added 11 points for Denver, which entered the game with several injuries and used just nine players. Derik Queen had 11 points and 12 rebounds, and Jeremiah Fears scored 11 points for the Pelicans, who are 0-4 under first-year coach Jamahl Mosley Murray made his first three shots -- all from deep -- and Denver shot 62% in the first quarter while building a 37-18 lead. Marvin Bagley 's runner gave Denver its largest lead at 44-22 with about nine minutes remaining in second quarter. The Pelicans struggled from the perimeter, hitting just 7 of 30 3-point attempts (23.3%). Denver played without Cam Johnson (ankle) and Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist) and continued to be without Julian Strawther and Spencer Jones . ESPN Research and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.title: 'A true professional': Jarred Vanderbilt leads Lakers' bench unit against Clippers
stories.summary: Jarred Vanderbilt starred in his bench role in the Lakers' 103-87 win over the Clippers at Intuit Dome. The offensive numbers are unremarkable. The impact was undeniable.
stories.detailText: Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt, left, battles Clippers guard Cam Christie for a rebound during the first half Wednesday. Vanderbilt collected seven rebounds off the bench. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times) By the time Collin Sexton arrived at the Lakers ’ practice facility Wednesday morning, just hours after a nearly three-hour slugfest against the Portland Trail Blazers , Jarred Vanderbilt was already deep into a morning workout. The Lakers were beginning a grueling five-game, seven-day stretch, but Vanderbilt was on the practice court in a full sweat at full speed. It’s no surprise to Sexton that Vanderbilt approached his long-awaited regular-season debut the same way Wednesday against the Clippers. “He’s always going to be ready for whenever his name is called,” Sexton said. “But that just shows a true professional.” Read more: Plaschke: LeBron who? Lakers happily shed the burden of departed star Vanderbilt starred in his bench role in his delayed season debut Wednesday in the Lakers’ 103-87 win over the Clippers at Intuit Dome. The offensive numbers are unremarkable: no points, one shot, one assist and a turnover. The impact was undeniable. The Lakers outscored the Clippers (1-3) by 22 points in his 21 minutes and two seconds he was on the court. Vanderbilt, who had seven rebounds, was one of three Lakers bench players to have a plus-minus of plus-21 or better Wednesday, along with Sexton (plus-23) and Sandro Mamukelashvili (plus-21). “The second unit, we have to come in and pick up where the starters left off,” said Sexton, who had 21 points, including 11 during the third quarter. “That’s the biggest thing. We got to come in and impact the game right away. We can’t come in and ease into it.” Vanderbilt’s energy helped the Lakers (4-1) win the rebounding battle for the first time this season. He didn’t waste any time after he subbed in with 3:26 remaining in the first quarter. On his first possession in the game, Vanderbilt repeatedly tipped a loose ball up in the air to keep it alive long enough for Austin Reaves to grab an offensive rebound. The 6-foot-8 forward did not appear in the Lakers’ first four games. He has been on the fringes of the Lakers rotation in part because his three-point shot is not reliable enough to offset his consistent defensive tenacity and energy. But with the Lakers struggling to find a backup center behind Walker Kessler , Lakers coach JJ Redick said Vanderbilt could get an opportunity to play out of position. Redick said he had previously had conversations with Vanderbilt about ensuring he would be in a position to succeed. Redick views Vanderbilt more as a wing or a forward than a center, where he occasionally played during 2025 after the Lakers traded for Luka Doncic and were shorthanded in the frontcourt. But with Kevon Looney being the only other full-time center behind Kessler this season, there could be moments when Vanderbilt plays the five by necessity, Redick acknowledged Wednesday. When Kessler wasn’t on the court Wednesday, Redick said the duo of Vanderbilt and the 6-foot-9 Mamukelashvili was “the best pairing in terms of having another big out there that can space and shoot and play-make.” Mamukelashvili had 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists and two steals in 30 minutes. Read more: Lakers, playing without Luka Doncic, have others step up in win over Clippers Looney, who was minus-eight in five minutes on the court against the Trail Blazers on Tuesday, did not play Wednesday. The three-time NBA champion offers a completely different skill set than Kessler at the position, and only one week into the season, Redick said the staff is still figuring out how Looney best fits into the team’s scheme. “You’re trying to figure out who you are as a group [at the beginning of the season],” Redick said. “You’re also, like, for a team with a lot of new guys, you’re trying to figure out what they are. You follow players for years. You can watch them play, and you got to figure out where they fit and how you can, again, put them in a position to succeed. So that’s still a work in progress with all regards.” The Lakers looked to bolster their depth at center by signing 7-foot center Lawson Lovering to a two-way contract Wednesday and waiving forward AK Okereke. Lovering was with Memphis’ G League affiliate, where he averaged 7.7 points, 7.1 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 30 games last season. He was undrafted out of Utah, where he finished his collegiate career that started at Colorado. Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: The reinvention of Zaccharie Risacher and his quiet eye
stories.summary: New Dallas Mavericks coach Dusty May’s approach is helping Zaccharie Risacher understand his role and his talent.
stories.detailText: MIAMI, FL - OCTOBER 26: Zaccharie Risacher #10 of the Dallas Mavericks drives to the basket during the game against the Miami Heat on October 26, 2026 at Kaseya Center in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Joe Murphy/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images On most teams, you find that one player. Especially for young players, there’s always someone who’s too quick for their own legs, too rushed, too out of control. It’s usually because their body is both quicker and more athletic than their brain realizes, and it can take a while for it to catch up. When I was a u16 player, we had one of those players. Too quick for her own legs, she would beat her defender, but throw the ball up, clanking it off the rim and then continue out of bounds, unable to stop. It was funny at times, but less useful in games. On the other side of the floor, however, she was a menace. Constantly getting a hand on passes on defense, throwing herself into rebounds. As crazy as it sounds, that reminds me of someone. Someone on the Dallas Mavericks, whose game has been looking too rushed. But then during the last few games, things seemed to improve. Zaccharie Risacher. Isaac Harris of the LockedOn Mavs podcast saw the same thing, and – luckily for me – asked Mavs coach Dusty May about it. “With Zacch, he’s done everything we’ve asked him to do. And sometimes, we want to see you more before we constrain you, or before we want you to do this or that. We want to evaluate you to see, because sometimes guys can do more than they’ve needed to in the past, because of their situation. After Houston, we painted a really clear picture of what we needed him to do. And he’s been very, very receptive.” I asked Dusty May about the game slowing down for Zaccharie Risacher & here’s his answer 🎥 – dallasmavs pic.twitter.com/7FJABXb1xR — Isaac Harris (@IsaacLHarris) October 26, 2026 And the coaching behind what they did to help Risacher slow down, especially his shot, is worth paying attention to if you’re into the technical (and mental) part of what goes into making a good basketball player and shooter: “(Today) he was really close to having as good of a stat line as his impact on the game,” May said after the Miami Heat win earlier this week. “His shots didn’t look rushed, it looked like he was playing with a much – we call it quiet eye – with a much quieter eye.” I saw a number of people questioning the term after this quote, asking if this was real and if May just made it up. But the concept of “the quiet eye” is in fact a very real thing, it even has its own Wikipedia page. When we talk about the quiet eye in basketball, we refer to the extended moment a good, usually elite player and shooter, stares at the rim – or space in the middle of the net – before shooting. An elite shooter locks eyes, if it had them, with the rim before getting a shot up. The more pressure, the longer the stare. It allows the shooter to focus, as well as visualize, where the shot will fall and how it’s going to look, the millisecond before you shoot. The better the shooter, the longer this moment is when the pressure is high. The quiet eye was one of my specialties as a player. I was a great shooter for a while there, and every time I was on a heater, I would see exactly where the ball fell just before I would shoot. It felt like prophecy, but it was more like visualization. And it works. We see examples of this with the best shooters in the league every day. When (brace yourselves, Mavs fans) Tim Hardaway Jr. is on a heater, he does this very well. Klay Thompson, of course, and Steph Curry. Bogdan Bogdanovic is another great example. And I’ve seen new Mav Tarik Biberovic do it in Fenerbahçe. Watch his stare at the rim from when he takes the first dribble: TARIK IS NOW 5/5 FROM DOWNTOWN! 🎯🎯🎯🎯🎯 Check out this buzzer three at the end of Q1 😮‍💨 @FBBasketbol pic.twitter.com/1CpBwQday6 — EuroLeague (@EuroLeague) April 28, 2026 What we have seen from Risacher recently, and what we will see even more going forward if he manages to incorporate this, is a much better three-point percentage. He has the mechanics down. The quiet eye could help him get the needed focus and get his numbers up fast. “Zacch is finding himself now,” Dusty May said . “He’s still so young. We really value and appreciate those plays. However many missed shots he had, he had twice as many loose balls, blocks, steals and rebounds and the ones that don’t show up.” Here’s a good example of what May mentions, this is just one play that stood out, where Risacher blocks a shot in a valuable possession for Miami with five minutes left, leading to a chance to secure important points on the other end for Dallas. THE BLOCK ➡️ THE AND-1 Risacher with the rejection, and Flagg with the basket plus the foul on NBA TV! 💪 pic.twitter.com/am5WQZhMih — NBA TV (@NBATV) October 27, 2026 Risacher is doing everything right. After the Miami game, he topped the leaderboard in stocks (steals and rebounds) with 16, an incredible number. Followed by Cooper Flagg (15) and Daniel Gafford (14), the Mavs players are really standing out early. Here’s another one of Risacher affecting the game directly with hustling and rebounding against the Oklahoma City Thunder Wednesday, cleaning up the possession after a missed shot. WATCH Zacch! pic.twitter.com/leDJVvWEz8 — MavsHighlights (@MavsHighlights) October 29, 2026 The Mavs coaching staff has been able to make this team play not only hard – as has been the strategy previously – but also smart. “I thought tonight he painted a masterpiece” Dusty May said after the OKC win. “He’s impacting every single possession… (Sasser and Risacher) are lighting a fire under us, and it’s been fun.” And it’s paying off, the whole team looks to have great chemistry, which May also mentioned: “Just to see how connected our group is. They’re so much for each other, it’s fun,” the Dallas Mavericks head coach said. “He makes us 15, 20 points better when he’s being active and getting steals and playing his defense,” Cooper Flagg said after the Miami game . “I have no doubt that his shots are gonna start to fall.” And the following game against Oklahoma, they did. Risacher made two out of three from beyond the arc, looking in control and maybe even utilizing that quiet eye, from the looks of it. Zacch beats the buzzer and drills the 3! pic.twitter.com/yw5TW3NEta — MavsHighlights (@MavsHighlights) October 29, 2026 And after Wednesday’s win over the Thunder, May revealed that the coaches see Risacher as something out of this world sometimes. “(Risacher) never gets tired. One of the assistant coaches, Coach Fodor, said he’s a cyborg. He comes out of a game playing five minutes that hard and he’s not breathing (hard), he’s just sitting there, you can’t even tell that he’s been playing…He’s kinda reinventing himself, where even though he’s not shooting nearly as well as he always has, he’s found a lot of value in other parts of the game.” The same day, the Dallas Mavericks announced that they had exercised their fourth-year team option on Zaccharie Risacher for the 2027-28 season. He’s reinventing himself with the guidance of good coaching in Dallas. And he has proved himself very important to winning for this team already. Zaccharie Risacher is in a good place.
