teamStories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - OCTOBER 28: Darryn Peterson #22 of the Utah Jazz drives past Devin Vassell #24 of the San Antonio Spurs during the first half of a game at Delta Center on October 28, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Without Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., and Jusuf Nurkic, I sat down to watch this game out of necessity rather than anticipation. Victor Wembanyama has mastered the art of beating up on teams that cannot match up physically, and I don’t think a center rotation of Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba was striking much fear into his heart. Let’s get this one over it, and be one day closer to the return of our all-stars. I am happy to report that my pessimism was, more or less, unfounded. Until the very end of overtime, the score fluctuated between a solid Jazz lead and a tie. What really made this an enjoying watch, however, was not the competitiveness itself but rather the means that led us to that outcome. The Jazz were carried by their three young pillars, and each was very consistently showing flashes throughout the game. Ace Bailey demonstrated strong mid-range scoring ability, with many sets run for him similar to what you’d expect to see run for a healthy Lauri Markkanen. Keyonte George was effective as the clear leader and offensive #1, scoring from all three levels. And Darryn Peterson, in my opinion, flashed the most ball-handling, shot-making juice that we have seen out of him thus far. Below you can find the clear highlight of the game: behind-the-back cross 👀 DP dials long distance ☎️ #TakeNote pic.twitter.com/WYkoSLIazf — Utah Jazz (@utahjazz) October 29, 2026 However, this underdog victory was not meant to be, for two primary reasons. The first, and most obvious, was the immense talent differential between the two squads. The Spurs essentially rolled out the team that nearly won them an NBA championship the year prior, and the Jazz put out a team that is arguably worse on paper than its 22 win 2025-2026 squad. Victor Wembanyama was the clear best player on the game, and he played like it. He seemed to sleepwalk his way to 36 points and 14 rebounds; this was not close to the intensity that he was displaying during the playoffs last season. They were missing their threes and Dylan Harper was struggling with efficiency, but San Antonio won the firepower game tonight, and it became clear once we hit overtime; the Jazz were struggling to find good shots (Brice made two threes, but they were tough ones), and the Spurs seemed to collectively “lock in” and take control. However, even with this talent difference, this loss was far from guaranteed, up until the bitter end. Instead, it felt like odd coaching decisions that put the final nail in the coffin. Will Hardy is taking his lumps adjusting to winning basketball just as much as any of the players, and it showed tonight. Injuries are surely a factor, but one consistent mistake he’s been making is playing entirely bench lineups for extended periods of time. Tonight, around the third quarter, the Jazz gave up a mini-run because Isaiah Collier was left as the lone ball handler with Ace, Keyonte, and Darryn riding the bench, Even less defensible was his overtime lineup choices. He began overtime with Isaiah Collier and Brice Sensabaugh as the backcourt with Keyonte and Darryn on the bench (we’ve been fined for less!), and even though Keyonte eventually came back in after a couple minutes of rest, Darryn Peterson did not find his way onto to the court for the remainder of the game. He explained (or at least attempted to explain) his rationale below: Hardy on why DP didn't play the last 7 mins of the game: "We gotta clean up execution, you know in those moments of the game you have to be able to execute the gameplan… in that moment I felt like it was better to go with Brice" Genuinely what is this answer? 😭 pic.twitter.com/RzCLUEyI5O — SleeperJazz (@SleeperJazz) October 29, 2026 This is rather incomprehensible to me. What better developmental reps can Darryn Peterson be given than those in overtime against the defending Western Conference champions? It’s not as if he was struggling tonight – he dropped an efficient-enough 18 points, and continued to provide impact on the margins. I understand the desire to get Sensabaugh in the game; he is, at this point, the superior isolation scorer to Darryn Peterson, and he had a bit of a hot hand. However, if Darryn is ever going to learn how to consistently score in isolation against strong defenses, he has to be given the opportunity to try his hand. Perhaps, on the bench, he was beginning to display some of the symptoms of a concussion that he may have sustained on a hard fit to the face from Victor Wembanyama. However, this is the only understandable excuse that I can conceive to explain why, on an injury riddled team in a game that went to overtime, our prestigious prospect played only 26 minutes. A few quick notes: I was a big fan of Josh Okogie’s activity tonight (but not a big enough fan to agree with him playing more minutes than Darryn Peterson). 9 rebounds in 28 minutes as a 6’4 guard is game altering. Mo Bamba was less eye-catchingly good, but he still provided perfectly respectable backup center minutes. He may be one of the better third string centers in the league when Nurkic returns. Ace’s touch is nice, but sometimes he does seem to rely on it rather than getting all the way to the rim. 0 free throws is quite unfortunate. What stood out to you from the Jazz’s game against the Spurs? Sound off below!

teamStories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - OCTOBER 28: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs moves around Jaxson Hayes #11 of the Utah Jazz during the second half of a game at Delta Center on October 28, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following an easy win over the lowly Kings, the Spurs faced a tougher foe in Utah Wednesday night, narrowly escaping with a 117-111 victory to extend their winning streak to three. With both Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out with injuries, the Jazz’ frontcourt was severely undermanned. The offensive burden was thus placed on Keytone George, who came out swinging. The shifty guard scored 10 quick points, helping the home team build a double-digit lead early in the game. San Antonio’s defense left much to be desired, often slow on closeouts and switches, giving Utah good looks at the basket. On the other end, the Jazz prevented Wemby from getting easy buckets by packing the paint. Still, it was only a matter of time before the big fella got loose, as the Spurs generated easy dunks for Wemby on the fast break and through pick-and-roll actions. San Antonio also ran successful inverted sets that used Wemby as the ball handler, taking advantage of his vision and the slashing ability of their guards. Even so, the Jazz answered every time the Spurs went on a run. San Antonio was only able to either tie the game or build a small two-possession lead, and the perimeter defense was not good enough to contain Utah’s explosive backcourt. Even after scoring on three consecutive possessions in crunch time, the Spurs allowed the Jazz to tie the game. With four seconds remaining in regulation, San Antonio had a chance at a buzzer-beater, but some slight confusion resulted in a desperate heave that gave me PTSD from the ending of game 2 of the finals. Overtime wasn’t much prettier from either side. Both teams had several disjointed possessions that somehow still ended up in the basket, and the Spurs pulled away by slowing down and getting Wemby some easy finishes at the rim. San Antonio built a multi-possession lead but still gave Utah life by conceding a wide-open three with less than a minute left, and it was a relief to finally hear the buzzer go off at the end. Game notes This was the Spurs’ third straight win, but the game still left me wanting more. San Antonio was disorganized for most of the night on both ends of the court, with the one silver lining being some of the offensive actions that they used involving Wemby as the hub. Other than that, there were a lot of rushed shots and possessions, and the point-of-attack defense also gave Utah too many great looks. Jeje reminded me that this was the second night of a back-to-back, so the team deserves some leeway, but there’s no denying that the team’s miles from their best at the moment. A big reason why the game was such a slog was due to Harper’s struggles. The young guard played his worst game of the season, shooting just 4-17 and finishing with 13 points. He did have 8 assists, but it seemed like he was forcing things on offense, and lost his assignment multiple times on defense too. Perhaps he was a bit too jazzed to go up against college teammate Ace Bailey, as Harper tried to iso and make a tough contested fadeaway against him once in the fourth. On the bright side, Wemby seems to be rounding into form. The Alien finished with 36 points on 14-25 shooting and 4-10 from deep, while also grabbing 14 rebounds and dishing out 5 assists. He was undoubtedly the difference Wednesday night. In a game that went to OT, Mitch Johnson elected to only play nine guys, including a short 5-minute stint from Carter Bryant. It was the first time this season that the Spurs played fewer than 10 guys, and it’s surprising considering that the match went long. Play of the game I loved how the Spurs used Wemby as a playmaking hub. It opens up so many different looks that can be exploited, and this is just one example of that. KJ ➡️ Vic 📺 @_daznus pic.twitter.com/9HKnpNLNpX — San Antonio Spurs (@spurs) October 29, 2026 Next game: vs Timberwolves on Saturday The Spurs will look to make it four in a row on Halloween against a Wolves team without Ant.

stories.title: Jags' home winning streak against Indy is 'weird, quirky' and a long shot to end Sunday
stories.summary: — Jaguars left tackle Walker Little perfectly summed up Jacksonville's 11-game home winning streak against Indianapolis.
stories.detailText: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- — Jaguars left tackle Walker Little perfectly summed up Jacksonville's 11-game home winning streak against Indianapolis. “It’s one of those weird, quirky stats that you see and you’re like, ‘That’s crazy,’” Little said. It has been an annual storyline surrounding this AFC South matchup for years — and might very well still be in 2027. The Jaguars (4-2), fresh off a bye week, will try to extend the streak when they host the struggling Colts (2-5) on Sunday. Indianapolis last won at EverBank Stadium in 2014 and will try to end the skid after a trying week in which the Colts traded team captain DeForest Buckner and longtime guard Quenton Nelson to start a rebuilding effort. “Regardless of circumstances, we have a job to do, and we’re excited for that challenge,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said. Indianapolis has dropped three in a row and 12 of 14 dating to last season. The Colts’ futility on the road against Jacksonville might be even more of a head-scratching slump. The 11-game slide includes a trip to London in 2016. Even in some of the Jaguars’ worst years — a one-win campaign in 2020 and a pair of three-win seasons — they managed to beat Indianapolis at home. “Meat and potatoes; keep the main thing the main thing and just play our brand of football,” Jaguars defensive end Josh Hines-Allen said. “And that’s all we worry about. The streak is the streak; it is what it is.” The Jags are playing just their third game in Jacksonville this season. They played consecutive “home games” in London, beating Philadelphia and losing to Houston, but gained ground in the division during the bye week because Houston, Indianapolis and Tennessee each lost. Jacksonville has won six consecutive regular-season games at EverBank Stadium, outscoring opponents 229-68 over that span. “It’s always nice to have a home-field advantage,” Jags coach Liam Coen said. “It’s not an easy place to come in and play, I don’t think. We play well at home, for sure. That’s something that you can lean into, but we haven’t necessarily talked about any streak or anything like that. “It’s the NFL — any given Sunday — and it can happen anywhere.” It hasn’t happened in Jacksonville for the Colts in a dozen years, and they are 10-point underdogs. It’s the first time the Jaguars have been a double-digit favorite in the series since 2017. “You just never know what can happen in this league,” Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner said. “You can’t be worried about all of the extra stuff. If you got a game that week, you prepare for the game each and every week no matter what’s going on the outside because, like I said, you never know what can happen in this league.” Need to know Indianapolis (2-5) at Jacksonville (4-2). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, CBS. Latest odds: Jaguars by 10. Against the spread: Colts 4-3; Jaguars 3-3. Last week: Colts lost at Vikings 16-10; Jaguars had a bye. Last meeting: Jaguars beat the Colts 23-17 on Dec. 28, 2025, in Indianapolis. Series record: Colts lead 28-22. Matchup to watch Jonathan Taylor against the NFL’s No. 1 run defense. Taylor has 587 yards rushing and eight touchdowns for the Colts this season. There was speculation he might get traded this week, but nothing materialized. Indy’s offense runs through him and will be tested in Jacksonville, which leads the league in rushing defense, averaging 72.2 yards a game and 3.23 yards a carry. Stats and stuff — The Colts have lost three in a row since winning consecutive games against Houston and Washington. — The Colts are 1/3 on the road this season, averaging 20 points a game. — Taylor is the last player to top 100 yards rushing against Jacksonville, finishing with 177 on the ground in a 26-23 overtime victory to end the 2024 season. — The Jaguars have won six consecutive regular-season games in Jacksonville, outscoring opponents by an average score of 38-11. — Jacksonville went 9-1 after its bye week last year, Coen’s first season. — The Jaguars have posted five first-quarter shutouts this season and have allowed three or fewer points in the first half of four games. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Falcons' Penix and Buccaneers' Mayfield aiming to help rebounding teams take control of NFC South
stories.summary: — Welcome to the NFC South, where inconsistency and seemingly disastrous starts to this season have not undermined the aspirations of the Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, Fla. -- — Welcome to the NFC South, where inconsistency and seemingly disastrous starts to this season have not undermined the aspirations of the Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers . After all, it is a division won by teams finishing with losing records two of the past four seasons, including a year ago when Carolina, the Falcons and Bucs all went 8-9. The Panthers by tiebreaker claimed their first title since 2015 and currently sit atop the standings again with a 3-3 record. Atlanta (3-4) and Tampa Bay (2-5) are lurking despite slow starts, with each hoping to bolster bids to take control of a wide-open race when the rivals meet Sunday. With Michael Penix Jr . at quarterback, the Falcons have won three of five following an 0-2 start that included a 31-point loss at Carolina. The third-year pro, who missed much of lase season with a knee injury, is coming off throwing for three touchdowns without an interception in a 29-20 victory over previously unbeaten San Francisco. The Bucs dropped four straight to begin the season, but are feeling better about themselves after riding a rejuvenated defense and relentless rushing attack to win two of their past three. Quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from missing three games due to a dislocated thumb to help lead last week's 43-13 rout of the division-leading Panthers, who yielded 258 yards on the ground. “I think that's our calling card,” Bucs coach Todd Bowles said. “We play a lot better when we run the ball successfully.” The Falcons are building a new identity, too. Since Penix took over at quarterback, Atlanta leads the NFL in scoring, though first-year coach Kevin Stefanski noted the team is also making strides in other important areas. “I just thought we were a very physical football team (against the 49ers),” Stefanski said. “That's got to be how we play. That's in our DNA. It's got to be what we're about.” Sunday will be a homecoming of sorts for Penix, who grew up in nearby Dade City, Florida, and attended high school in Tampa. “It's exciting, and I imagine I should have a lot of people coming to the game,” the Falcons quarterback said. “My mom, she usually knows that head count. But it's gonna be exciting to be able to get out there.” Need to know Atlanta (3-4) at Tampa Bay (2-5) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m., EST, Fox. Latest odds: Buccaneers by 2 1/2. Against the spread: Falcons 3-4, Buccaneers 2-5. Last week: Falcons beat 49ers 29-20; Buccaneers beat Panthers 43-13. Last meeting: Falcons beat Buccaneers 29-28 on Dec. 11, 2025, in Tampa, Fla. Series record: Falcons lead 33-32. Matchup to watch Penix vs. Buccaneers defense. After missing the first two games of the season, Penix has thrown nine touchdown passes with only one interception. Atlanta is 3-2 with him as the starting quarterback. Tampa Bay has 10 sacks in the past two games after only having six in the previous five games. Stats and stuff — Each of the last six games between the division rivals has been decided by six or fewer points. — Falcons WR Drake London leads the NFC with 256 yards after the catch. — Atlanta RB Bijan Robinson leads the NFL with 704 rushing yards. He leads all running backs with five games of at least 100 scrimmage yards. — Penix has completed at least 72% of his passes in each of Atlanta’s three wins. — Atlanta has allowed only 62 quarterback pressures, tied with San Francisco for the lowest total in the league. — Falcons TE Kyle Pitts has four TD catches in the last three games. — The Buccaneers are 0-4 at home vs. 2-1 on the road. — Tampa Bay has won two of three games following an 0-4 start, rushing for 241 yards in a victory at Dallas and 258 yards at Carolina last week. — Mayfield only threw 11 passes in his return from injury against the Panthers last week, completing seven with one TD and no interceptions. Tampa Bay finished with 49 rushing attempts. — RB Bucky Irving is averaging 4.7 yards per carry and leads Tampa Bay with 558 yards and four TDs. — LB Yaya Diaby had three of Tampa Bay's five sacks against Carolina. — The Buccaneers have the NFL's third-ranked defense and are one of four teams allowing fewer than 100 yards per game rushing (77.3) while also limiting opponents to less than 300 yards per game total offense (294.7). The Vikings, 49ers and Seahawks are the others. ------ AP Sports Writer Charles Odum in Atlanta contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Jets' Brownlee says he was benched for missing meetings, but 'good' for Sunday
stories.summary: Jets nickelback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was benched last Sunday because he missed multiple mandatory meetings and was fined by the team.
stories.detailText: FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets nickelback Jarvis Brownlee Jr . was benched last Sunday because he missed multiple mandatory meetings and was fined by the team, he told ESPN on Thursday. Brownlee said he couldn't recall the amount of the fine, except to say he was notified in a letter from the team. He said he missed "more than one" meeting, adding that he understood the discipline. "No doubt, no doubt," he said. "Just accountability." Asked why he missed the meetings, Brownlee said, "It was just something in-house, some things I had to get right." Brownlee, the Jets' starting nickel, was inactive for the New York's 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins . He was replaced by rookie D'Angelo Ponds . Coach Aaron Glenn declined to say why he benched Brownlee, adding that he wanted to keep the reason "in-house." Brownlee said he's "good" for this week. From indications, he will be active Sunday when the Jets (2-5) host the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4). The Jets acquired Brownlee from the Tennessee Titans early in the 2025 season. The Jets traded a 2026 sixth-round pick for Brownlee and a 2026 seventh-round pick. Brownlee, a 2024 fifth-round pick by Tennessee, has appeared in 13 games for the Jets. This season, he has 14 tackles and one sack in six games (241 defensive snaps).

stories.title: Cowboys look for rare winning streak under Brian Schottenheimer in visit from Cardinals
stories.summary: — Sustainability is the next challenge for the Dallas Cowboys, who have just one winning streak in nearly a season and a half under coach Brian Schottenheimer.
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Sustainability is the next challenge for the Dallas Cowboys , who have just one winning streak in nearly a season and a half under coach Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas (3-4) begins a stretch of four home games in five weeks with a visit from Arizona on Sunday after a 38-21 road division win against two-time defending NFC East champion Philadelphia. As strange as it sounds, the Cowboys did what they should have against the Eagles. Philadelphia's offense is decimated by injuries, and the beleaguered Dallas defense still needed three quarters to figure out how to get stops. The Cowboys had the second-worst rushing offense in the NFL before Javonte Williams went for a career-high 155 yards rushing among the team's 204. A two-week rut ended for one of the league's best offenses, with season highs in yards and points. Now Dallas has to do it again. “It’s a business where you have to be consistent with your execution, with your performance,” said Schottenheimer, whose only winning streak was a three-game run last season. “And I think we've been lacking that at times. Another good week, another opponent coming in there with a lot of challenges that they’re going to present, but it’s more about us and the lack of consistency.” Arizona's 2-5 record is irrelevant because it has nine victories in the past 10 meetings with Dallas. Each of the past three times the Cardinals won, they lost at least 14 games that season. A year ago, it was the only victory in the final 15 games . The Cardinals ended a four-game losing streak with an upset of the Los Angeles Rams on the road two weeks ago, only to lose to Denver 30-16 for their 10th consecutive defeat at home . Arizona is 2-2 on the road this season and is perfect in four visits to AT&T Stadium, which opened in 2009. “Where I always try to put my focus is that this is a week-to-week league,” first-year coach Mike LaFleur said. “I want these guys to be where their feet are. The highs that they felt (against the Rams), the lows that they felt after this last game. Once you reset, you learn from it on those Mondays, you get right back to work, and you work to be 1-0. Good, bad, or anything in between, I don’t try to look past that.” Need to know Arizona (2-5) at Dallas (3-4) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox. Latest odds: Cowboys by 6 1/2. Against the spread: Cardinals 3-4, Cowboys 4-3. Last week: Cardinals lost to Broncos 30-16; Cowboys beat Eagles 38-21. Last meeting: Cardinals beat Cowboys 27-17 on Nov. 3, 2025, in Arlington, Texas. Series record: Cowboys lead 56-36-1. Matchup to watch The rushing offense against the rushing defense for both teams. The Cowboys and Cardinals are averaging fewer than 100 yards rushing per game, but Dallas is coming off its second 200-yard game since Schottenheimer took over as coach and play-caller. Arizona has played the past two games without rookie No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love (ankle), but undrafted fifth-year man Bam Knight has been a capable fill-in with a 5.8-yard average on 22 carries in those games. Dallas is 31st in the NFL in rushing defense, allowing 145.7 yards per game. The Cardinals are 23rd at 126.3. Stats and stuff — Cowboys QB Dak Prescott had his 80th game with multiple touchdown passes by throwing for three scores against the Eagles. That broke a tie with Tony Romo atop the team's career list. Prescott also has the most games with at least three TD passes at 43. — Dallas' Williams is tied for the NFL lead with eight touchdowns rushing and has scored in five consecutive games. — Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb leads the NFL with 81 targets, the most through seven games in franchise history. He has a pair of two-TD games this season after not having any a year ago. — Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams tied his career high with three tackles for loss against the Eagles. He had his team-leading third sack. — Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr ., acquired in a trade with Pittsburgh on Oct. 1, is set for his home debut. He was a late scratch with an illness in the 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay at AT&T Stadium on Oct. 8. — Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett threw for 261 yards with two TDs and ran for a score against the Cowboys last season in his first win as the team’s starter. He has a 3-16 record over 1 1/2 seasons. — The Cardinals have an NFL-leading 21 drives of at least 10 plays, and also lead with 18 of those ending in points. They are fourth in the league in average time of possession at 32:16. Dallas gave up a TD drive of 9:16 in Philadelphia. — Cardinals TE Trey McBride leads the NFL with 59 catches, the most by a tight end in league history through a team’s first seven games. He can join Antonio Brown and Cooper Kupp as the only players with at least seven catches in 10 consecutive games. Brown has the record at 14 in a row. — Arizona kicker Chad Ryland is 9 for 9 on field goals over the past two weeks, including all of his team's points in the 18-16 win over the Rams. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Longtime football coach June Jones, pioneer of run-and-shoot offense, dies at 73
stories.summary: Longtime college and pro football coach June Jones, who helped popularize the run-and-shoot offense, has died at 73.
stories.detailText: Longtime college and pro football coach June Jones, who helped popularize the run-and-shoot offense, has died at 73. The University of Hawai'i confirmed the death of Jones, who played quarterback for the Rainbow Warriors and later served as an assistant and head coach from 1999 to 2007. Jones was the Atlanta Falcons ' coach from 1994 to 1996 and also led teams at SMU , the CFL's Hamilton Tiger-Cats and the XFL's Houston Roughnecks. He was the Chargers ' interim coach for 10 games in 1998. Jones turned down the chance to remain Chargers coach and returned to Hawai'i, where he became the school's all-time winningest coach with a 76-41 record. He guided Hawai'i to conference titles in 1999 and 2007, when the team started 12-0 and earned its first berth in a BCS bowl (Sugar) behind star quarterback Colt Brennan. At Hawai'i, Jones also coached Timmy Chang, who became the NCAA's all-time passing yards leader and now serves as the program's head coach. Jones then helped revive SMU's program, leading the Mustangs to four consecutive bowl games, the team's first postseason opportunities since receiving the "death penalty" for NCAA violations in 1987, and consecutive division championships in 2009 and 2010. "Coach Jones helped restore a winning tradition on the Hilltop," the school said in a statement. "Our thoughts are with his family, friends and the countless players and coaches whose lives he touched." An Oregon native, Jones finished his college playing career with Portland State, where he was introduced to the run-and-shoot by Mouse Davis, the scheme's innovator. Jones played five seasons for the Falcons and one in the CFL before beginning his coaching career at Hawai'i, overseeing quarterbacks in 1983. He coached in the USFL and CFL before landing his first NFL job coaching the Houston Oilers' quarterbacks under Jerry Glanville in 1987. Jones later served as Falcons offensive coordinator before taking over as head coach following the 1993 season.

stories.title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 8): Colts fan confidence plummets amid roster overhaul
stories.summary: Fan confidence drops sharply as the Colts continue losing and trade away two of their biggest stars.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Carlie Irsay-Gordon, owner of the Indianapolis Colts looks on before the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest SB Nation Reacts survey shows a significant decline in confidence among Indianapolis Colts fans, with just 31 percent believing the franchise is headed in the right direction . That’s a substantial 16-percentage-point drop from last week’s 47 percent, suggesting that whatever optimism emerged following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard has quickly begun to fade. Last week’s results suggested that fans were beginning to regain some hope following Ballard’s dismissal, despite the team’s embarrassing loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. However, another disappointing performance against the Minnesota Vikings did little to improve the mood surrounding the franchise. Indianapolis fell 16-10 on Sunday, dropping to 2-5 and extending its losing streak to three games. While the defense kept the Colts competitive throughout the afternoon, another ineffective offensive performance raised further questions about Shane Steichen’s ability to turn things around with Daniel Jones under center. The situation became even more complicated Tuesday when Indianapolis traded two of its most accomplished veterans, sending eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. In return, the Colts acquired a 2027 third-round pick, a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection. The moves represented a significant shift in the organization’s approach, suggesting that Indianapolis is now prioritizing the future rather than attempting to salvage an increasingly disappointing season. While accumulating draft capital could prove beneficial in the long run, losing two of the franchise’s best players undoubtedly creates additional uncertainty. Nelson had been a cornerstone of the offensive line since 2018, while Buckner remained one of the defense’s most reliable contributors (maybe the most reliable). Their departures leave significant holes on both sides of the football, and with wide receiver Josh Downs reportedly requesting a trade as well, there is growing speculation that additional veterans could be moved before the November 10 trade deadline. The decline to 31 percent reflects a fan base with plenty of reasons to question where the organization is headed, although the results do not tell us which developments influenced individual voters. Some may welcome the decision to begin rebuilding through the draft, while others are understandably frustrated with the prospect of another lengthy transition after years of disappointing results. With Indianapolis also lacking its first-round selection in the 2027 NFL Draft following the Sauce Gardner trade, whoever takes over as general manager will face considerable challenges in rebuilding the roster. For now, the Colts still have ten games remaining and an opportunity to show some progress under Steichen. However, with the franchise increasingly focused on the future and uncertainty surrounding several of its remaining stars, restoring confidence among fans will likely require more than a few organizational changes. Indianapolis needs to demonstrate that it has a clear plan for returning to contention, something that has been missing for far too long. FanDuel Sportsbook

stories.detailText: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. But the deals have already kicked off. The Giants traded for Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy , the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr . to the Cowboys, the Eagles sent center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens and the Texans acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . The Colts traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , too. And the biggest deal yet happened on Oct. 29, with the Titans sending defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears and landing two first-round picks in return. We're tracking all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. The most recent deals will be added at the top. More coverage: Transactions | Depth charts Oct. 29 Titans trade DT Simmons to Bears Bears get: DT Jeffery Simmons , 2028 fifth-round pick Titans get: 2027 first-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 first-round pick The Bears are acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The Titans are receiving 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-round pick from the Bears in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick, the sources told Schefter. Simmons, 29, signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension with $100 million guaranteed with the Titans in June. He is under contract through the 2030 season. The Colts will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from the 49ers, sources said. Colts trade G Nelson to Seahawks Seahawks get: G Quenton Nelson Colts get: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick The Colts have agreed to trade eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Nelson is on an expiring contract, and the Colts are opting to get back draft capital now before they could lose him in free agency. The Texans sent 2027 second- and sixth-round draft picks to the Cardinals for Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round selection, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Harrison reunites with his former Ohio State QB C.J. Stroud in Houston. The Eagles had moved Jurgens to left guard after Landon Dickerson was placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. stories.summary: I am bewildered as to why so many people (writers, bloggers, podcasters, fans, etc) are down on the Vikings mainly because the offense is failing to score enough points for their liking. I contend that the Vikings are actually doing an excellent job running their offense especially considering the injuries they have h…
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images I am bewildered as to why so many people (writers, bloggers, podcasters, fans, etc) are down on the Vikings mainly because the offense is failing to score enough points for their liking. I contend that the Vikings are actually doing an excellent job running their offense especially considering the injuries they have had to navigate whilst trying to incorporate Kyler Murray into the offense. They are not turning it over and they have one of the top time of possessions in the NFL thus far. This is allowing their defense to stay well rested and wreak havoc. But they get not credit for any of that. Here are some numbers for time of possession and rushing yards per game … Team | TOP | TOP Rank | Rush Yds/G | Rush Rank | Past SOS | REM SOS | Games Played Chicago Bears | 35:30 | #1 | 154.29 | #1 | #31 | #21 | 7 Minnesota Vikings | 32:43 | #2 | 119.33 | #12 | #24 | #26 | 6 New York Giants | 32:32 | #3 | 116.71 | #15 | #30 | #31 | 7 Arizona Cardinals | 32:15 | #4 | 96.00 | #23 | #6 | #5 | 7 Indianapolis Colts | 31:59 | #5 | 117.57 | #14 | #19 | #16 | 7 Tampa Bay Buccaneers | 31:55 | #6 | 146.43 | #3 | #10 | #8 | 7 Jacksonville Jaguars | 31:29 | #7 | 112.83 | #18 | #13 | #27 | 6 Seattle Seahawks | 31:21 | #8 | 113.71 | #17 | #12 | #2 | 7 (Note: TOP is Time Of Possession; for SOS ranks, 1 is the hardest and 32 is the easiest.) Also, the Vikings defense ranks #1 in the NFL for the opponent’s average starting field position. Opposing offenses are forced to start their drives at an average of their own 25.3-yard line, This is helped by the dudes that put their foot on the ball. Through 6 games, the Vikings have punted 27 total times, pinning their opponents inside the 20-yard line on 10 of those opportunities (37.04% of their punts). This does not take away from the offense prioritizing clock management and not turning the ball over in their own territory. … seems to me that KOC is actually doing an outstanding job keeping things afloat while dealing with the injuries. The defense is fantastic but they also are getting helped by the offense keeping the ball longer and not giving up short fields too often. Now some might argue that other teams have had to deal with injury too. Not like the Vikings though. Minnesota Vikings Kyler Murray QB — left early in Week 1; missed Week 2. Jordan Mason RB — injured his thumb in Week 1; missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 Christian Darrisaw LT — left Week 4 with a concussion; missed Week 5. T.J. Hockenson TE — left Week 5 after three snaps with a concussion; missed the next game, with the Week 6 bye in between. Justin Jefferson WR — left Week 3 with an ankle injury; missed Week 4. Jordan Addison WR — missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury. Jauan Jennings WR — missed Week 2. Donovan Jackson LG — suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. The only other team to come close has been the 0-6 Chargers Los Angeles Chargers David Njoku TE — reported absences in Weeks 3–7; exact game-by-game status needs verification. Kayode Awosika LG — reported absences in Weeks 3 and 5–7. Joe Alt RT — reported absences in Weeks 4–5. Tyler Biadasz C — reported absences in Weeks 4–5. Rashawn Slater LT — reported absences in Weeks 5–6. Ladd McConkey WR — left Week 1 early; reported out in Week 6. Tre Harris WR — left Week 5 early; reported out in Weeks 6–7. Omarion Hampton RB — reported out in Week 3. For me, when you take all of this into context, the fact that the team is undefeated is outstanding work. I realize that the wailing and gnashing of teeth will continue on in regards to the JJ McCarthy trade. I do not think it will ever die down this season and probably not for at least one or more future seasons. If he stayed, the odds of him playing this year were low. He would have had to surpass Wentz as the backup? If he did not play then what would his trade value have been in the 2027 offseason? Should they have gotten more than a 5th? Well yeah. Why not? But from what team? What team would have traded more for him now? It’s easy to say but harder to identify the team willing to give up more knowing that he was injured often (including this 2026 preseason) and had fallen to third string. The best thing is that JJ McCarthy now has a chance to play and try to put his game on tape so that he is able to secure a future contract. I’m OK with the return but always want more in trades. What will the Vikings do in 2027? Well, if not Murray, then they could try for Mac Jones. Deshaun Watson is likely going to be released due to his contract and he is doing well this year. Daniel Jones could get released too. That is possibly four options there. Could Lamar Jackson be on the trade block? That might be the dream scenario. Overall, I think the team is headed in the right direction. I think they will have a decent QB for next season and right now my money is on Murray returning. I would not mind that if he plays a little better the rest of the way. A short 2 yr deal plus maybe bring in Anthony Richardson to back him up. Now you know why I am not GM eh? News Alert The Bears traded two first round picks for Jeffrey Simmons! Wow! I love it! Looks like Jonathan Taylor is not going anywhere either. According to Shefter, the Colts do not “inherently” want to trade Taylor Schefter: Colts owner doesn't want to trade Taylor Would you trade a 2027 2nd, 2027 5th, and a 2028 3rd for Taylor? I would without hesitation. Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason are both free agents and there are no good backs as free agents next year either. The team will likely have to spend a first or second to get a decent back in the draft. I’d rather have Taylor if possible. If the Vikings do trade for him before the game this week they would owe him about 5.3M in salary for the rest of the season.. If they wait until after this game and before the next game (makes the most sense now) then they would owe him 4.8M in salary for the rest of the season. The Panthers' four cornerbacks for tonight are Will Lee, Chau Smith-Wade, Malcolm DeWalt and Marco Wilson. The team announced they signed DeWalt to the 53-player roster on Thursday. He signed to the practice squad last week and arrived Sunday. He was a healthy scratch in all six games on the Falcons' active roster this season. The Panthers elevated Wilson and guard Jake Curhan from the practice squad to the game-day roster. Wilson was the most experienced of the six corners on the practice squad this week, with 64 appearances and 37 starts, mostly with Arizona. The former Florida product has also spent time with the Patriots, Bengals and Dolphins before signing to the Panthers' practice squad earlier this month. Curhan played 13 games for the Panthers last year, with one start in the regular season against the Rams. Against Green Bay last year, he subbed into the game and played both guard spots in the same game. He joins Damien Lewis and Torricelli Simpkins III at the position for tonight against the Packers.

stories.title: Reacts Results: Oh we of little faith
stories.summary: What do the Panthers have to do to earn a little credit? How about start by producing consistent results.
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 4: Robert Hunt #50 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates after a touchdown against the Detroit Lions during an NFL football game at Bank of America Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Our Week 7 surveys found 96% of Carolina Panthers fans confident in the current direction of the franchise. 82% of y’all were predicting a winning season. It’s amazing how one truly awful game can change so much of what we think about our favorite team. That’s just what happened during and after the Tampa Bay Buccaneers completely dismantled every positive narrative that Panthers fans were spinning and buying. A win tonight against the Green Bay Packers would go along way towards recovering some of that lost goodwill, but let’s not get ahead of ourselves. We wouldn’t want to be too much like the Panthers on Sunday. Unlike what many of the coaches and players repeated after the game, this is not something that just needs to be flushed away. You don’t lose half of your fanbase during one game and say “oh well.” Both the game and the reactions have left a sour taste that will require time to get over. It’s not out of line of what was expected entering this season. Consistency is all most of us have been asking for since the Ron Rivera days. Instead, we get to follow high highs with incredibly low lows. I’ll keep watching, but I won’t start believing until we see sustained change. How about you? stories.title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly: Bengals 35, Ravens 13
stories.summary: A tale of two halves by the Bengals against the Ravens last Sunday.
stories.detailText: Two halves, two completely different football teams. For 30 minutes on Sunday, the Bengals looked like they were still on their bye week. For the next 30, they looked like the best team in the AFC North. The final score was 35-13. Cincinnati improved to 4-2 and finally got that first division win. But a game like this deserves a full breakdown, warts and all. Let’s get into it. The Good Second-half Joe. After halftime, Joe Burrow went 16-of-18 for 249 yards and four touchdowns, which is a perfect 158.3 passer rating. The Bengals scored on five straight possessions and put up 298 yards and 19 first downs in the second half alone. Burrow finished 22-of-30 for 292 yards and four scores. He has 15 touchdown passes through six games, his most ever at this point in a season. Tee Higgins shows up when it counts. Higgins was shut out in the first half. In the second, he caught six passes for 148 yards, including a 44-yarder and the 13-yard go-ahead touchdown. That’s his 17th career 100-yard game, and he went over 6,000 career receiving yards in the process. No. 1 talks, No. 1 delivers. Burrow credited Ja’Marr Chase for lighting a fire at halftime. Chase then put the exclamation point on it with a 2-yard touchdown in the fourth, his 10th career score against Baltimore. The defense slammed the door. Baltimore didn’t score after halftime. It managed five first downs on six second-half drives and turned it over on downs on a fourth-and-2 at the Bengals’ 12 while trailing by a point. The Bengals scored on the very next drive. For the day, Huntley was sacked four times, with Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence II and rookie Cashius Howell (his first career sack) all getting home. Demetrius Knight Jr. added an interception. Derrick Henry, bottled up. Henry ran 17 times for 45 yards, a 2.6 average, and the Ravens averaged 3.1 yards a carry as a team. When you hold King Henry under 50 yards, you’re doing something right up front. Tight ends and the punter. Mike Gesicki (6-yard touchdown, his fourth straight game with a score) and Drew Sample (16-yard touchdown) each found the end zone. Ryan Rehkow dropped all four of his punts inside the 20. The Bad The run game is still stuck in neutral. Chase Brown had 11 carries for 39 yards, and the backs combined for 61 yards on 18 carries. Samaje Perine did punch in a touchdown. The passing game carried this one, but you can’t count on Burrow throwing for four touchdowns in a half every week. This offense needs to be able to run the ball when it has to. Huntley had a career day. A backup quarterback, with Lamar Jackson out for a third straight game, threw for a career-high 298 yards against this defense. Zay Flowers caught eight passes for 137 yards, including a 48-yard screen for a touchdown on Baltimore’s first drive. The second half was great. But the secondary gave up too many explosive plays early, and a better quarterback makes them pay. Baltimore let them off the hook. Baltimore had two red-zone trips in the first half that ended in field goals instead of touchdowns, and the Ravens committed 10 penalties for 57 yards. They also were in chip-shot field-goal range to begin the fourth quarter but opted to go for it on fourth down and failed. If they cash in on even one of those trips, this is a much tighter game. The Ugly That first half. There’s no way to dress this up. At halftime: Burrow was 6-of-12 for 43 yards. The Bengals had two first downs and crossed midfield once. Baltimore outgained them 258 to 59. The Ravens ran 39 plays to Cincinnati’s 19 and held the ball for 22:20 of the first 30 minutes. Baltimore converted 8 of 11 third downs, its most in a first half since 2018. Higgins didn’t have a catch. FOX19’s Jeremy Rauch called it “arguably the most incompetent half in the Joe Burrow era,” and I’m not going to argue with him. The defense couldn’t get off the field, and the offense couldn’t stay on it. That’s how you end up down 13-0 to a team starting its backup quarterback. The Bengals got away with it this time. They won’t against Buffalo, Kansas City, or anybody else they might see in January. The comeback deserves the headlines, but the coaching staff needs to spend this week figuring out why this team keeps coming out flat. Injuries and Erick All Jr. on I.R.: The safety position got banged up in this one, with Bryan Cook, Kyle Dugger, and Jordan Battle all getting dinged up in one form or another. Cook and Battle returned, but Dugger has a lingering injury. All landed on Injured Reserve this week, with the fear being that he yet again tore the ACL in the knee he did so twice before. It’s a sad end to his season, after coming back ahead of schedule this offseason and integrating himself well into the offense.

stories.title: Are the next two Cardinals games the last for Josh Sweat? Budda Baker?
stories.summary: The season just isn’t going very well
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams is hit by Josh Sweat #10 of the Arizona Cardinals during the game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The Arizona Cardinals won 18-16. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals had hopes for a decent season this year. The prognosis was to win between six and eight games this year, then add a few more wins in the second season under new head coach Mike LaFleur. Then hopefully, by Year 3, the roster would start making waves and qualify for a playoff berth. RELATED: TWO CARDINALS AMONG BEST CANDIDATES TO MOVE Of course, this was the same plan for former head coach Jonathan Gannon. But instead of a postseason berth, Gannon’s final year ended with breaking the franchise record for the most losses in a single season with 14. So, is this a teardown process for the Cardinals? It is normal for a new head coach to come in and clean house, then bring in “his” type of players. On opening day this year, there were 23 new bodies on the active roster, and several more listed on the practice squad. After the first seven games, the Cardinals find themselves at 2-5-0 and once again in last place in the NFC West Division. Their schedule this year is brutal, despite being a last-place division finisher in 2025. Coming up, they have games against the Dallas Cowboys, Kansas City Chiefs, plus divisional games against the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and the league-leading San Francisco 49ers. All of these games could be losses. They could also get beat by mediocre clubs such as the Washington Commanders and the Philadelphia Eagles. Arizona plays the Cowboys this weekend, and then the rubber game against the Seahawks. Both games are on the road in front of very hostile crowds. If they lose both, should they begin the process of starting over? Rebuilding? Part of every team’s process of a new beginning is to get rid of their highest-priced players. For the Cardinals, that short list includes DE Josh Sweat and S Budda Baker. Sweating it out EDGE Josh Sweat was the main part of the Cardinals’ pass rush last year, as he balled out in the first year of his new contract to the tune of 12 sacks, 17 QB hits, and 28 pressures, among other stats. But this year, he has lost his partner in crime, DT Calais Campbell, who wasn’t re-signed. Campbell had 6.5 sacks on his own plus 16 QB hits and 18 pressures. He was a huge disruptor in the opposing team’s backfield on passing downs. Now, in all fairness, Arizona GM Monti Ossenfort did select Campbell’s replacement in this year’s NFL draft when he took DT Kaleb Proctor out of Southeastern Louisiana. He is one of those rare defensive tackles who can provide a pass rush and isn’t just a gap plugger. And he ran a 4.71. Then, Proctor tore his meniscus during training camp and was ruled out for the entire season. The plan was for Proctor and DT Walter Nolen to dominate the middle and take pressure and double teams off of Sweat. But Nolen has been in the medical ward off and on. So, how is Sweat doing this season with the additional attention placed on Campbell? 16 total tackles, 3 tackles for loss, 4 QB hits, 0 pass defenses, 0 forced fumbles, 0 fumble recoveries, 0 interceptions, 8 pressures, 4 hurries, 2 knockdowns, and 0 missed tackles. What do these numbers say to you? Pro Bowl prospect? Marginal talent? Sweat was real good friends with former Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon, who is now the DC with the Green Bay Packers under LaFleur’s brother, Matt LaFleur. When Gannon got fired for losing 26 games in the past two seasons, it became a problem for Sweat. Now, he said it wasn’t an issue, as he stated in Sports Illustrated : “People think I only came here for one reason, and that was Jonathan Gannon, and yeah, that made the decision easier for me. But I know the guys that were here. I love the way they play. There was a lot of noise in the offseason, but I didn’t respond purposely. I just wanted to see how far people’s imagination could take it.” This has gained some steam on social media, so just to provide some clarity: #AZCardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat is not being traded. Not to the #Packers or anywhere. Carry on… pic.twitter.com/bImuZfvWLq — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) June 3, 2026 During training camp, there were rumors that because Gannon was fired, Sweat had demanded a trade. That may or may not have been the truth, but nothing more came of it. Then Sweat stayed out of all training camp, showed up the week before the first game, and has played ever since. But there is no way he is the dynamic pass rusher he was last year. Sweat is one of those EDGE rushers that has good to very good numbers every year on a consistent basis, but he isn’t going to blow the doors off of any offensive coordinator’s game plan the way a guy like Myles Garrett or Micah Parsons may generate interest. Now in his ninth NFL season, he only has a single Pro Bowl. . @1053SS on the Cowboys potentially trading for Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat: "I'm out on Josh Sweat for what it will cost, and I'm out for what he will do for this defense…" pic.twitter.com/LHpOGh0DGE — 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) October 29, 2026 For two months, all we have heard is how Sweat will be a trade deadline candidate. If Ossenfort had traded him during the offseason, Arizona just might have gotten a good haul for him. Perhaps even a first-round draft pick. But now? What? Would the team jump at the first third-round offer that is dangled? Then there is the money issue. Sweat is in the second year of a four-year $76 million deal, with $38 million guaranteed. This year he has a cap hit of $16.4 million. The final two years of the contract rise to $23.6 million. The market for defensive linemen has already begun. The Indianapolis Colts traded DE DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers. The Tennessee Titans traded star DL Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. The only other pass rushers rumored to be traded before the November 10 deadline are Los Angeles Chargers EDGE rusher Khalil Mack and Sweat. The big question for Ossenfort: Which is better for the Cardinals this year and in following seasons? Have Josh Sweat on the roster, or have whichever rookie player that third-round draft pick creates? The Budda Man Safety Budda Baker is a fan favorite, and the desert is his only NFL team. He was a second-round selection in the 2017 NFL Draft out of Washington and has since gone to eight Pro Bowls, been named to the NFL All-Rookie Team, voted First Team All-Pro twice, Second Team All-Pro twice, and was the NFL solo tackles leader in 2019 (104). He had a career-high 164 total tackles in 2024 and has had 100+ tackles in six of his 10 seasons. So, why is Baker on this list? Anyone? Don’t ask him. He appears to be happy with the Cardinals. He told ESPN Arizona : “My approach is I’m here. I’m here. I want to win. I want to be here. And I’m just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I’ll still be here. If not, I mean, it’s a business. I understand at the end of the day, and that’s it.” Perhaps it is the fact that he is a senior member of the roster. Or maybe it is the amount of money the Cardinals are paying him. He is in the final year of a three-year, $54 million deal in which his cap hit this year is $19.2 million. Ossenfort will have to sign Baker to another extension or trade him. But in fairness, it seems like every year, when the media begins to write articles about the impending NFL trade deadline, Baker’s name seems to leak out as a possible candidate. Baker has noticed: “My name has been attached to trade rumors for like five, six years now. So, at the end of the day, I’m here, be where your feet are. I’m happy to be a Cardinal and just focus on getting a “W” this week versus the Cowboys.” The NFL is in the entertainment profession. It is also a business with so many moving parts and pieces. And those pieces get moved around a lot. NEWS: Cardinals S Budda Baker told me today he has not asked for a trade but has also not asked not to be traded. He hopes to stay in Arizona after the dust of the trade deadline settles but he said he understands the NFL is a business. My story from today:… — Josh Weinfuss (@joshweinfuss) October 29, 2026 Jeremy Fowler of ESPN stated this about the Cardinals moving Baker: “A few wins won’t camouflage Arizona’s transitional state — and it needs draft capital to finish the rebuild. Baker, who has seven consecutive Pro Bowls and has 3.5 sacks on the season, could help get the Cardinals some extra picks. Long a favorite in coaching circles, Baker would garner strong interest. People I’ve talked to believe the Cardinals should try to get something for Baker.” Okay, first of all, let’s do a correction. Baker has been to the Pro Bowl eight times, not seven. And secondly, why should the Cardinals “try to get something” for Baker? What is wrong with where he is? He already has 44 tackles, and it is just seven games played. He had 120 last year and 164 the year before, so it’s pretty clear his production isn’t waning. And he is an extremely durable player. That in itself is pure gold in a violent atmosphere like professional football. It would be shocking if Ossenfort actually traded away Baker’s productivity. And for what? Are we talking about Arizona receiving a first-and second-round draft pick? Or just another third-round rookie?

stories.title: Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown return for full practices
stories.summary: The Lions got running back Jahmyr Gibbs and wide receiver Amon-Ra St.
stories.detailText: The Lions got running back Jahmyr Gibbs and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown back on the practice field Thursday. Gibbs sat out on Wednesday with a shoulder injury and St. Brown has an ankle injury, but both of them were able to fully participate in their return to practice. That bodes well for both of them being in the lineup against the Vikings this weekend. Defensive lineman Tyliek Williams also returned as a full participant after missing Wednesday with an illness. Defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, defensive tackle Alim McNeill, left tackle Penei Sewell, and defensive end DJ Wonnum all returned to work after resting Wednesday. Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw (ankle) were listed as limited for the second straight day. Running back Jacob Saylors (neck) moved from limited to full participation.

stories.title: Lions, Vikings injury report: All 7 starters return to practice on Thursday
stories.summary: Taking a closer look at the Lions and Vikings Thursday injury report for Week 8.
stories.detailText: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (14) scoring a touchdown against New Orleans Saints with running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) during the overtime at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (4-2) and Minnesota Vikings (6-0) were back on the practice field on Thursday as they prepare for their Week 8 NFC North showdown. The Lions returned all seven starters to practice on Thursday, as planned, including Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle). Let’s take a look at Thursday’s injury report and get you up to date with what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . N o practice None All 53 players on the Lions’ active roster practiced Thursday. Limited practice CB Ennis Rakestraw (ankle) S Kerby Joseph (Knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 19 Rakestraw was forced from Week 7’s game against the Packers, and while that typically means no practice early in the week, he hasn’t missed a practice yet. While limited, he is on track to be available for his rotational outside cornerback role again this weekend. Joseph is slowly being worked back into football shape, but has stacked two practices as he moves through the injury evaluation process. He still has 19 days remaining in that window, and the Lions will use all of them if they deem he needs them in order to be ready. Considering he hasn’t been on the practice field in basically a year, it’d be a stretch for him to be ready for the Vikings; the Dolphins game could also be in question, meaning his first game back could end up being against the Patriots in Germany. Full practice RB Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) — upgraded from no practice on Wednesday RB Jacob Saylors (neck) — upgraded from limited practice Wednesday WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) — upgraded from no practice on Wednesday OT Penei Sewell (rest) — upgraded from no practice on Wednesday DT Alim McNeill (rest) — upgraded from no practice on Wednesday DT Tyleik Williams (illness) — upgraded from no practice on Wednesday EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (rest) — upgraded from no practice on Wednesday EDGE DJ Wonnum (rest) — upgraded from no practice on Wednesday Gibbs was unexpectedly added to Wednesday’s injury report due to a shoulder injury, but it did not restrict him from getting back to practice on Thursday. After practice, Gibbs told reporters he was surprised to see he was listed as questionable on an alert on his phone and downplayed the injury. “It said ‘questionable’ I don’t know what was questionable. I was confused. It popped up on my phone, and I’m like ‘What the hell?’” Gibbs said. “Yeah, just got dinged up a little bit, a little shoulder thing, but I’m good, though. I’m straight.” Lions coach Dan Campbell will likely address the injury at his Friday press conference, but there are no indications this will impact his ability to contribute against the Vikings. Saylors was also unexpectedly present on the Lions injury report, but his getting in two practices so far this week is a good sign he’s on track to be available on Sunday. With DeAndre Carter only starting his second game at kick returner, the Lions would feel more comfortable if Saylors could also start alongside him. St. Brown tweaked his ankle in Week 7, and while he missed practice on Wednesday, he was back in the fold on Thursday, following the plan Campbell detailed earlier in the week. St. Brown is expected to be good to start on Sunday. “It’s good,” St. Brown told reporters Thursday. “It just got stepped on throughout the game. So it just got swelled up a little, but I’m all good.” Sewell, McNeill, Hutchinson, and Wonnum got the veteran rest day on Wednesday, and as Campbell suggested earlier in the week, they returned to the practice field on Thursday. The Lions hope the extra day of rest will give their superstars a little more juice against the Vikings this Sunday. Williams technically missed practice Wednesday due to an illness, which is common in Michigan this time of year, but he was able to get back to work Thursday. He is expected to be good to go this weekend. Viking s’ Thursday injury report Coming soon.

stories.title: A.J. Brown injury update: Patriots wide receiver misses more practice
stories.summary: Will A.J. Brown play in Week 8? Latest injury update for the Patriots wide receiver dealing with a couple of lower body injuries.
stories.detailText: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown 's comeback may have lasted all of two games. Brown did not practice with the rest of his team on Thursday, Oct. 29, according to multiple reports. The star wide receiver was already limited in practice on Wednesday, Oct. 28 with a couple of lower body injuries, but his practice status has regressed as the week has progressed. The former Philadelphia Eagles wideout has already missed four games this season after a high ankle sprain in Week 1 landed him on injured reserve . Brown has played in three out of the Patriots ' seven games since New England sent a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick to Philadelphia to acquire the receiver . As a Week 8 clash with the Miami Dolphins approaches, Brown appears to be at risk of missing a fifth game this year. Here's what we know about the three-time Pro Bowler's status: PATRIOTS NEWS: Mike Vrabel has blunt response to reported $250,000 fine: 'Talk to the league' A.J. Brown injury update The 29-year-old Brown did not practice on Oct. 29 as he deals with injuries to his ankle and knee. NFL Media and ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported on Oct. 29 that the Patriots initially listed Brown on their injury report on Oct. 28 as a limited participant with a knee injury. The team has since added an ailing ankle to the receiver's injury designation as he misses practice for the first time since his Week 6 return. Brown has appeared to be less than 100% recovered in his first two games back off of injured reserve. The wideout made his comeback in Week 6 against the Jets, where he promptly dropped two of his 10 targets and finished the game with just three catches. In Week 7 against the Bears, Brown caught three of his six targets but was 0-for-2 on contested targets and tallied just one yard after the catch, per Pro Football Focus. Brown's status for Week 8 remains unknown. Patriots WR depth chart Here's how things would look in the Patriots' receivers room if Brown is able to go on Sunday, Nov. 1: A.J. Brown DeMario "Pop" Douglas Kyle Williams Efton Chism III That is a notably short list of healthy receivers – and Brown may not be healthy. New England already has the other two of its top three receivers out on injured reserve: Romeo Doubs with a shoulder and Mack Hollins with a calf. The Patriots do have four more wide receivers on their practice squad to fill out their depth, especially if Brown is unable to play in Week 8: Ryan Miller, Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon and Chandler Brayboy. Miller is in his fourth season and appeared in five games for the Dolphins this year before they waived him. Dorner and Dixon are both UDFA rookies. Brayboy is a second-year receiver yet to make his NFL debut. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: A.J. Brown injury update: Patriots wide receiver misses more practice

stories.title: Should the 49ers offer the Jets a Jeffery Simmons deal for Garrett Wilson?
stories.summary: To keep the draft picks, or to not. That is the 49ers question.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the best players at his position signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension this past summer. That player was traded Thursday morning to the Chicago Bears in exchange for a 2027 and 2028 first-round pick. The Titans also sent a fourth-rounder this year, while the Bears sent back a 2028 fifth-rounder. It’s a deal you make when Jeffery Simmons just turned 29. The Bears are telling you they believe Simmons will provide more value than the three picks they dealt away over the next three years, at least. Could the San Francisco 49ers pry away Garrett Wilson from the New York Jets? The situation is similar. The Jets are 2-5. Wilson signed a four-year, $130 million contract extension in July 2025. The selling point to the Jets The Jets will incur a dead cap if they trade Wilson. According to Over the Cap, trading Wilson would cost $6.75 million in dead money through 2029 and $4 million in 2030. Jets fans will cite that as a primary reason the Jets won’t part ways with their budding star receiver. There’s the other side of the coin: the cap space you save. You’d save $16.5 million in 2027, and over $29 million during the next two years. This was Wilson last Sunday: A frustrated Garrett Wilson has some words for Geno Smith on the @nyjets sideline as he's been a non-factor with the Jets trailing the winless Dolphins 21-14. Smith appears unmoved. pic.twitter.com/esmJHlbXi7 — Glenn Naughton (@JNRadio_Glenn) October 25, 2026 On Wednesday, Wilson said he didn’t want to be traded, but he does want to win. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Wilson’s frustrations as “ a healthy tension ” on Thursday. From a long-term perspective, it seems silly for a team projected to use one of their first-round picks in 2027 on a quarterback to trade away a top-flight receiver like Wilson. The Jets haven’t had any problems moving the ball in their last two games against divisional opponents. Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. has back-to-back 100-yard receiving games. Their other first-rounder, Kenyon Sadiq, isn’t the most dangerous tight end on the roster. That goes to the second-rounder in ’25, Mason Taylor. The Jets already have three first-round picks in the ’27 draft. Adding another would give them the ammunition to at least attempt to replace Wilson. You’re reminding them they can move the ball without Wilson while selling them on the value of buying two first-rounders to replace him. It’ll also open up cap space down the line for a team that’ll already have the third-most next year with over $85 million — and that’s with Wilson’s contract on the books. Why the 49ers should be aggressive buyers Trent Williams is 38. George Kittle is 33. Mike Evans is 33. DeForest Buckner is 32. Christian McCaffrey is 30. You don’t know how much longer Nick Bosa’s body will hold up. We’re a year removed from the ultimate Ironman, Fred Warner, missing double-digit games because of a freak accident. He turns 30 in November. The 49ers brass would be foolish to think this iteration of the 49ers — arguably the best of the decade — will hold up for another 20+ game season after this year. It’s a haughty assumption, especially from a team that was robbed of a Super Bowl appearance after their quarterback sustained a fluke injury in the NFC Championship Game earlier this decade. I’ve been a staunch advocate for the 49ers to avoid trading for a run-of-the-mill receiver. Josh Downs doesn’t make you a Super Bowl contender. Wilson is a needle mover. He surpassed 1,000 yards receiving in his first two seasons with Zach Wilson throwing him the ball. If that isn’t enough of an argument, then I’m not sure what would convince you that he’s the real deal. I could clip together Wilson running out routes where he breaks the cornerbacks’ ankles, releases off the line of scrimmage with the defensive back hopping the opposite direction of Wilson, or him making acrobatic catches down the field. There isn’t a route Wilson can’t run. Wilson becomes the future of the 49ers. Like the Bears — if we’re acting under the guise of the deal being multiple first-rounders — the Niners are banking on Wilson producing more —albeit far more expensive — than their two first-rounders in the next two years would. But you’re paying for that by acquiring Wilson at this contract. You get to skip past the “teach this guy how to play football” phase. There is no learning curve. You’re getting one of the best players at his position with the skill set you’d create in a lab for a Kyle Shanahan offense. The 49ers have fallen on hard luck before signing Evans. Swinging for the fences on Wilson would help the team wash their hands of the Brandon Aiyuk disaster, provide peace of mind without having to hold their breath in the future to see if Ricky Pearsall stays healthy, and take pressure off De’Zhaun Stribling to replace Evans down the line. The 49ers’ first-round draft history under this regime doesn’t come close to Wilson’s caliber. You’re removing the guessing game with a win-now player who also provides stability at a position you’ve whiffed on in recent years. It’s a rare NFL opportunity for a team like the Niners to capitalize on a player entering his prime who is visibly unhappy. It’s a big if, as there are plenty of uncontrollables for the 49ers. Everybody has a price.
