teamStories.summary: Growing pains were expected with rookie coaches Klint Kubiak and Rob Leonard, but the 4-game skid shows how bad it is
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The game of football is decided in the trenches — more often than not. And the Las Vegas Raiders are habitually losing that battle. And, as a result, the team is in a four-game freefall and are 3-4 overall after a torrid 3-0 start to the 2026 season. The Silver & Black’s most recent outing — a 35-21 shellacking at the hands of the visiting Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday — where the team was outgained on the ground 199 yards to 48 yards, was the latest example of the ineffectiveness in the trenches. The Rams battered the Raiders at the line of scrimmage — offensively and defensively — sprinting to a 28-6 lead at halftime and the deficit threw everything into disarray for Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak and his coaching staff. The lack of production in the ground game reeked of not only ineffectiveness but also coaching ineptitude and the reeling Rams used the Raiders as a get-right game showcasing the balanced offensive attack and aggressive defense that Kubiak wants from his football team. “Yeah, well, we’re not going to run the ball until we stop the run. Until you make the game competitive,” Kubiak plainly said on Monday when asked about the constant theme of Las Vegas improving the run game and run defense. “You can’t be in the fourth quarter chasing points and expect to be a good run team. So, you need attempts, and in order to get those attempts, then we have to stop the run, and we have to keep our opponent out of the end zone.” In those four-straight losses, Las Vegas defense is getting sliced through like hot knife through butter allowing 656 total rushing yards while the offense has struggled to produce 223 rushing yards. The 199 yards yielded to the Rams ground game was the high mark during that span and the 72 yards the Raiders run game produced in the 30-27 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 4 being the most Kubiak’s crew produced. Through seven games, Las Vegas owns the third-worst ground game with 523 yards total and a 3.0 yards per carry average (second-worst). Only the Green Bay Packers (419 yards) and Cincinnati Bengals (487) are worse in that department — those two teams are 4-3 and 4-2, respectively, by the way. While there are fleeting moments breakaway runs, Raiders starting running back Ashton Jeanty (stats) and rookie backup Mike Washington Jr. (stats) run into the backs of offensive linemen or are taken down behind or at the line of scrimmage. The #Raiders were dominated up front. When you can't stop the run or run the ball, you can't win. pic.twitter.com/cm0C0g0mOv — JT The Brick (@JTTheBrick) October 26, 2026 Despite being stonewalled on the ground, Kubiak’s aerial attack is producing, albeit in one-dimensional fashion. Led by veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins, the Raiders passing game is the second-best group in terms of yardage (1,883) and atop the league with 16 touchdowns. The Rams have the most passing yards (1,919) and the San Francisco 49ers and Bengals are tied for second in touchdowns with 15. To showcase the imbalance that Kubiak spoke about above, Las Vegas is sixth with 266 passing attempts compared to 16th in rushing attempts with 174 totes. And the disparity in production from those two areas are crystal clear. It’s great that Las Vegas has the fifth-best offense with a total of 183 points, but the team also has the second-worst defense allowing a total of 197 points (a -13 point differential, the winless Los Angeles Chargers (-61) and 2-5 Arizona Cardinals (-66) are worst teams in this department). All of that showcases this isn’t an aberration for the Raiders. After the team’s defeat to the Chiefs, I noted Kubiak’s quickness to take ownership of the team’s shortcomings as admirable . Admitting an issue is the first step to fixing it. However, the inability to get the ground game going remains a glaring liability. Even considering there would be growing pains with a rookie head coach in Kubiak and his chosen defensive coordinator Rob Leonard (who is also a neophyte at his post), not being able to run the ball and stopping opponents from doing is a total collapse that exceeds realistic expectations. This highlights a disconnect in coaching, player execution, and overall roster quality. Of that trio, the first two are within Kubiak’s and his coaching staff’s control while the third can be truly bolstered next offseason with another round of free agency and draft. Sure the general manager John Spytek can explore the trade market before the November 10 deadline, but the Raiders roster issues in Year 1 of the Kubiak era requires more than just that. “Well, no one’s coming to help us. We’ve got to figure it out ourselves as a coaching staff with the players, and we have to complement each other as well because to we’ve got to start the game a lot faster offensively,” Kubiak said in the postgame press conference after the loss to the Rams. Great punch out by JJ Pegues 🔥 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ulY8ligD9N — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Accountability is key and it’s present in both the Raiders coaching staff and roster. “Absolutely, yeah. And there’s conversations like that every game, whether you’re winning and losing. There’s always hard conversations at halftime, making adjustments, holding people accountable. That’s part of every team,” middle linebacker Nakobe Dean said after the loss to the Rams. “For sure, for sure, I got a lot of belief. I got a lot of faith in this team,” Dean added. “We got a lot of great players. We just got to put it together. We got to play as a team. We got to play as one. We can’t be all individual mercenaries out there.” The taking action to change the behavior and fixing specific problems remains an issue. Opponents continue to load the box to stymie the Raiders ground game and daring the team to beat them over the top — which Las Vegas hasn’t consistently done even though it’s gotten quality production from tight end Brock Bowers and wide receiver Tre Tucker. Communication issues on defense compound a young Raiders secondary as tight ends, deep routes, and short passes in the flat are wide open too often. There there’s poor tackling technique and angles (Pro Football Reference charts Las Vegas with 41 missed tackles, eighth most int he league and a 8.5 percent missed tackle rate as a team) that make the soft zone coverages even more ineffective. And because of the consistent shortfalls, tempered expectations are in order. The luster of the 3-0 start is gone and reality has set in like heavy fog. Three victories and four losses in the initial seven games is progress for a rookie head coach, so kudos to Kubiak. And while his expectations from his football team are elevated and gargantuan, this is Year 1 of his tenure. And the Raiders are no paragon of quality depth and talent roster-wise — I don’t think anyone will say otherwise (and if you do, can I have a sip of that Kool-Aid?). “Yeah. I think from our perspective as players and coaches, that’s not something that’s on our mind. What’s on our mind is win the next game, and we’ve played very talented teams and played much more competitive games than that, being the Chiefs and the Bills,” Kubiak responded when asked about this not being an overnight rebuild and did the last four loses show there’s a gap that needs to be made up. “Yesterday, when you start the game that slow, you put yourself in position to be behind that much, you don’t give yourself a chance to win.” "Fernando [Mendoza] is gonna play at some point, it's not gonna be this week." Raiders HC Klint Kubiak names Kirk Cousins the starting QB vs. the Jets. pic.twitter.com/38npWXO5PH — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 26, 2026 Kubiak and Co. clearly have winning as the prime directive as it continues the 2026 campaign and the next opportunity is this coming Sunday at the New York Jets. The ultra-productive Cousins remains the starting quarterback and Kubiak continues to seek offensive balance and improved outings from Leonard’s defense. To do so, Leonard must quell the 35.8 points per game surge his unit has allowed the last five weeks and bring back the all-for-one effort the Raiders defense showed when the team rattled off three-straight wins. The team was communicative and playing both aggressive and fast in that span which included an impressive nine takeaways. Since then, however, Las Vegas has forced just three turnovers. Leonard’s group is tied for second-best in the NFL in that regard (the Packers are tops with 13 takeaways). Leonard was naturally defiant when asked if the bevy of takeaways mased his defense’s weaknesses during the 3-0 start. But it’s quite clear without them, opposing offenses are toying with his cover-four and coverage-matching system. Kubiak, when asked the same question, was more diplomatic in his response noting the turnovers forced is complementary football. And that’s what’s been lacking when it comes to the Silver & Black. Like Kubiak said, no one is coming to help them, and in order to snap the losing streak, it’s up to both coaches and players to rekindle that lost art of complementary play. Lest the losses continue to stack.

teamStories.detailText: The New England Patriots attempted to add to their defensive line this week, but ultimately failed to do so. One of six teams to put in a waiver claim on former Las Vegas Raiders defender Jonah Laulu, they were undone by their record being superior to that of the other five potential claimants. Besides the Patriots, the Tennessee Titans, Miami Dolphins, Houston Texans, Indianapolis Colts and New York Jets also tried to bring Laulu on board, according to a report by NFL insider Jordan Schultz. The 1-5 Titans were awarded the 26-year-old on Wednesday. Laulu entered the league as a seventh-round draft pick by the Colts in 2024 but was waived after his rookie training camp. He ended up with the Raiders as a waiver claim, and since then played 39 games with 22 starts for Las Vegas. Along the way, he registered 5.5 combined sacks — including 0.5 in five games this season. However, Las Vegas’ new coaching staff under Klint Kubiak did not view him as an integral part of the team’s defensive rotation. After playing 68% of defensive snaps in 2025, he was on the field for only 23% so far this year. His release earlier this week did not come as a particular surprise. For the Patriots, the move presented an opportunity to add another pass rusher to their interior defensive line. At the moment, the group consists of Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, Cory Durden, Joshua Farmer, DaQuan Jones and Leonard Taylor; Eric Gregory and Jeremiah Pharms Jr. offer additional depth on the practice squad. In total, New England has 52 players on its active roster, meaning that no follow-up move would have been necessary had Lautu been claimed. The Patriots are traveling to Miami this week to take on the Dolphins in a 4:25 p.m. ET matchup on Nov. 1.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images If a postseason elimination game in Week 8 exists, the contest between the Las Vegas Raiders and New York Jets is it. The 3-4 Raiders and 2-5 Jets are only separated by a game and both teams are on the outside looking in at the AFC playoff picture , meaning neither club can afford another loss to stay “in the hunt” at the halfway point of the season. So, the three key matchups below will be crucial to keep any (albeit slim) playoff hopes alive. Johnson vs. Cooper While wide receiver Garrett Wilson is still the Jets’ top option in the passing game, leading the team with 37 catches for 444 yards and three touchdowns through seven games, Wilson’s production has significantly decreased over the last two weeks. He’s logged just six catches for 70 yards in the last couple of contests combined. Part of the reason for that is rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. returned from injury. After suffering a sprained ankle while hauling in his first NFL catch (a 30-yarder) and just five snaps into his professional debut, Cooper has been on a tear since returning from injured reserve in Week 6. He had six catches for 103 yards and a touchdown against the New England Patriots and then went for five, 115 and one versus the Miami Dolphins last Sunday. According to Pro Football Focus , the Indiana product has spent 67.8% of his pass snaps in the slot this season, where seven of his catches (58.3% of his season total) and 188 yards (75.8%) have come from. Additionally, his 5.37 yards per route run from the slot ranks third among NFL wide receivers who have at least six targets on the inside. Granted, that’s where missing four games is a slight advantage, as that figure could come down with a bigger sample size. But the overall point is that Cooper has been a problem for opposing nickelbacks. Meanwhile, the Raiders have a veteran nickel in Taron Johnson, who has been stingy in slot coverage this season. Of corners with at least 41 coverage snaps on the interior, he ranks fifth in yards per coverage snap allowed at 0.63, giving up 10 catches on 16 targets (62.5%) for 96 yards and a touchdown, per PFF . That being said, Johnson has benefited from a few off-target throws, recording just one PBU and logging a subpar 54.0 coverage grade . Where this matchup could get really interesting is after the catch. Despite missing time, Cooper ranks seventh among slot receivers with 111 YAC and second in YAC per reception (15.9, minimum six targets) and has forced three missed tackles, according to PFF . Johnson is 15th among nickels in total YAC allowed ( 58 ) and is typically a sure tackler, recording his first miss of 2026 in Week 5. However, he has four failed tackle attempts in the last three games. While Wilson is the name people recognize most in the Jets’ receiving corps, Cooper is the hot hand right now, which makes Johnson’s impact on Sunday even more important. Bowers vs. Fitzpatrick Brock Bowers’ impact on the Raiders’ offense doesn’t need much explanation. He missed the first two games of the season and still leads the team in targets (52) and receptions (34) while trailing wide receiver Tre Tucker for the team lead in receiving yards (474 to 455) and touchdowns (four to three). That’s led to the tight end getting the ‘WR1’ treatment from defenses, where Las Vegas’ opponents often put their best coverage defender on him. For New York, that player is versatile defensive back Minkah Fitzpatrick. The nine-year veteran has made five Pro Bowls and been a first-team All-Pro three times throughout his career and is still playing at a high level. On 148 coverage snaps this season, he’s only been targeted nine times and has yielded just five receptions, per PFF , with a PBU and an interception thrown in the mix. However, he is prone to giving up explosive plays in coverage, allowing 122 receiving yards for 24.4 yards per catch, including 20-, 37- and 42-yard grabs. Granted, Fitzpatrick has only given up on catch to a tight end — an 18-yarder to Colston Loveland in Week 4 against the Chicago Bears — and the Jets rank 13th with 0.186 EPA per target to tight ends this season, per Sumer Sports . But Bowers is not a typical player for the position, and New York is coming off games where Hunter Henry had four catches for 48 yards, four first downs and a touchdown, and Greg Dulcich went for five grabs, 85 yards and five first downs. Part of the issue for Gang Green, though, is that none of Henry’s and Dulcich’s targets came against Fitzpatrick. In other words, expect to see the two perennial Pro Bowlers line up across from each other often in Week 8. Jeanty vs. Sherwood Of course, the Raiders’ run game is struggling, ranking second to last in the NFL with negative 0.27 EPA per rush, according to Sumer Sports . That likely isn’t changing against a Jets defense that currently has the eighth-best EPA per rush at negative 0.12 . Still, a matchup between a running back and a linebacker can be a big one on Sunday with the implications it has in the passing game. Ashton Jeanty has almost as many receiving yards as rushing yards so far this year ( 312 to 328 ) and currently leads all running backs in receptions (34, tied with Christian McCaffrey), receiving yards and receiving touchdowns (three). He’s also the most targeted (43) back in the league and is tied for seventh with Jahmyr Gibbs in yards per route run (1.91), according to PFF . Meanwhile, Jamien Sherwood has been a quality coverage linebacker in New York this season. He has a solid 65.5 PFF coverage grade that ranks 25th at the position and is tied for 20th with a seven percent forced incompletion rate. Additionally, Sherwood has given up 25 or fewer receiving yards in five out of seven games . However, he has yielded 236 yards on the campaign, with over half (127) coming in Week 3 against the Detroit Lions. The former college safety had an especially tough time against Gibbs, who hauled in five catches on five targets for 47 yards against him, per PFF . Lions’ backup running back Sione Vaki also had an 11-yard catch versus Sherwood in that contest, for good measure. Also, the matchup extends to a pass protection battle. Sherwood has registered 12 pressures on 49 pass rushes — the third-most among off-ball linebackers — and Jeanty has given up three pressures on 37 opportunities . However, the latter has been much better in that department lately, allowing just one pressure in the last four games while recording three PFF pass-blocking grades in the high 70s to low 80s three times during that stretch. In other words, this matchup has a high variance of outcomes. In full disclosure, Tyler Linderbaum vs. T’Vondre Sweat and DJ Glaze vs. David Bailey were also considered key matchups. However, according to Eric Allen of the Jets’ website , head coach Aaron Glenn said Sweat is week-to-week with a knee injury that caused him to exit last week’s game early, and Bailey is dealing with a “lingering” groin injury that could keep him sidelined on Sunday. Neither player participated in Wednesday’s practice.

teamStories.summary: — Las Vegas Raiders fans are getting restless, while New York Jets fans are fully frustrated.
teamStories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — Las Vegas Raiders fans are getting restless, while New York Jets fans are fully frustrated. Something's got to give. Right? The struggling squads square off Sunday at MetLife Stadium with each looking to get their season on track — as outside noise starts to grow louder. The Raiders (3-4) have dropped four straight after a surprising 3-0 start and some fans are calling for rookie Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 overall pick in April, to take over at quarterback to provide a spark. Kirk Cousins hasn't been bad, by any means — he leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes — and coach Klint Kubiak shut down any chatter this week by saying the 38-year-old veteran would remain under center and “there is no controversy.” “I’ve seen the production," Kubiak said. "The production’s there. But it’s a team game, so we’ve got to produce together in order to win football games.” Same for the Jets (2-5), who have dropped two in a row, including a 28-25 defeat at home last Sunday to previously winless Miami. That loss fired up an already simmering seat under Aaron Glenn, who's 5-19 as New York's coach and might need an impressive run over the final two months to save his job. “I’ve been around a lot of good coaches and a lot of good leaders and I’ve said it a lot, I think A.G. is one of the best I’ve ever been around," center Josh Myers said. "I still believe that and I’ll continue believing that.” Geno Smith will see some familiar faces across the field after being the Raiders' starting quarterback last season, when he led the NFL with 17 interceptions. He was acquired by the Jets in the offseason and has respectable numbers — 10 touchdown passes, two INTs, 1,623 yards passing and a 70% completion rate — but the offense is struggling with consistency. Perhaps this week New York, ranked 23rd in yards per game, can get things going while facing a Las Vegas defense that's tied for 29th in yards allowed. “They’re a really good team and we’re not taking them lightly,” said Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby , who added that he likes where the Raiders are at mentally. “Adversity reveals who you are. ... You can’t fall into the negativity. You've got to be positive, regardless of what the world wants you to feel like. "So the only way to change that is go win and go be at your best, so that’s what we plan on doing.” Need to know Las Vegas (3-4) at New York Jets (2-5) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox. Latest odds: Jets by 1 1/2. Against the spread: Raiders 5-2; Jets 4-2-1. Last week: Raiders lost to Rams 35-21; Jets lost to Dolphins 28-25. Last meeting: Jets won 16-12 on Nov. 12, 2023, in Las Vegas. Series record: Raiders lead 27-20-2. Matchup to watch Raiders' running game vs. Jets' run defense. Las Vegas enters averaging 74.7 yards rushing per game , ahead of only Green Bay (59.9). New York ranks 24th against the run, giving up 127.7 yards per game — and there might be some extra motivation. Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty said Wednesday he thinks Las Vegas can get its ground game going this week because the Jets have "a couple guys out there that don’t really want to tackle, but I’m not going to say names.” Stats and stuff — The Raiders are the 13th team in the Super Bowl era to open 3-0 and then lose their next four games. Carolina and Denver in 2021 were the most recent teams to do it, and only Tampa Bay in 2000 made the playoffs. Five of the previous 12 teams had their losing streaks extended to five. — Las Vegas is tied with three others with 25 or more points in five games. The Raiders scored that many points only once last season, a 30-29 overtime loss to Jacksonville. — While running the ball has been a problem for the Raiders, so has stopping the run. Las Vegas is 30th in rush defense. allowing 143.6 yards per game. — The Raiders are tied with Seattle and Tampa Bay for second in the NFL with 12 takeaways. — The Jets have been outscored 107-6 in the final two minutes of the first half during the past two seasons under Glenn. — Jets rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr . is the third player in NFL history with at least five receptions, 100 yards receiving and a TD catch in two of his first three career games, joining Don Looney (1940, Philadelphia) and Bobby Johnson (1984, Giants). — WR Garrett Wilson had just two catches for 26 yards on three targets last week and has expressed frustration about his usage. Wilson's 37 receptions are still second in the AFC and his 51 targets are tied for fourth in the conference. — New York has scored on its opening drive in three straight games. — Jets rookie edge rusher David Bailey , who's dealing with a groin injury , joins Pro Football Hall of Famer Brian Urlacher the only players since 2000 to have at least 5 1/2 sacks and 35 tackles in their first seven NFL games. ------ AP Sports Writer Mark Anderson in Henderson, Nevada, contributed. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images While explaining why he is sticking with veteran Kirk Cousins as his starting quarterback, Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak pointed out the team is still in the AFC playoff mix. To remain in the mix, the Raiders must win at the New York Jets on Sunday. After starting the season 3-0, the Raiders have dropped four straight game. Falling to 3-5 at midseason would be staggering for the Raiders for several reasons. The Jets are 2-5 and aren’t a good team. The Raiders, whose three wins this season have come against teams with a combined 3-16 record, must take advantage of this schedule break. Their next three games are at the San Francisco 49ers, at home against the Seattle Seahawks and at the Denver Broncos. Those three teams are a combined 15-6. There is little room for error in this stretch. The Raiders’ schedule does ease down the stretch, but the key is for Las Vegas not to create a hole they can’t dig out of. There are currently nine teams in the AFC with running records. Seven teams advance to the playoffs. The Raiders are the only team in the conference at 3-4. Six teams have two or fewer victories in the AFC. If the Raiders want to stay close the playoff chase, they must win at New York. Dropping to 3-5 after a 3-0 start would be devastating for a team and it could propel the team into becoming trade sellers before the November 10 deadline. So, for a lot of reasons, this is a crucial week for Kubiak’s team.
